name: Apple Cinnamon Compote
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Apple Cinnamon Compote; 1-1/2 pounds apples; 1-1/4 cup water
ingredients:
1 tablespoon lemon juice


 

Buttermilk & Honey Flapjacks
2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions:
Apple Cinnamon Compote


	Peel and core apples then cut them into eighths. 
	Place them in a shallow wide saucepan with ¼ cup of water, brown sugar, 1 tablespoon of honey, and cinnamon over medium heat. 
	Bring to a boil then reduce heat to low. Simmer and stir until apples are soft and fragrant (about 10 minutes).
	Add the remaining 1 cup of water and ½ cup of honey, raise to medium heat, and stir to combine. 
	Bring mixture to a boil and continue cooking for 20-25 minutes or until the apples have turned golden and syrup has thickened. 
	Stir in the lemon juice. 


 

Buttermilk & Honey Flapjacks


	Combine Kodiak Cakes Buttermilk Power Cakes Mix, water, honey, and cinnamon. 
	Heat a griddle or skillet over medium-high heat with ½ tablespoon of butter. 
	Add ¼ cup of the flapjack batter to the skillet and cook until bubbles form on top and the bottom is golden. Then flip and cook on the other side until golden.
	Set aside the cooked flapjacks and add another ½ tablespoon of butter to the skillet.
	Once the skillet is hot, add another ¼ cup of the flapjack batter to the pan and repeat process until you’ve made 8 flapjacks (using all the batter). 
	Serve the flapjacks with apple compote on tip, and maple syrup for drizzling.
description: Sometimes your scrumptious flapjacks call for apple cinnamon compote that’s worth drooling over. Finish your homemade breakfast with a heap of spiced, tart flavors that put you in the festive fall mood. Each bite warrants seconds. Trust us—it’s that good...

Combine the dry breading ingredients in a shallow bowl. In another bowl, whisk together the Kodiak mix and water until smooth to create the wet batter.

One at a time, dip the pickle chips into the wet batter, letting any excess drip off. Then, gently coat the pickle chip with the dry breading mixture and carefully place it in the hot oil. Careful not to overcrowd the pan.
Fry for 2-3 minutes or until golden brown and crispy.
Remove the fried pickle chips with a slotted spoon and place on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.

Serve hot with ranch dressing, spicy mayo, or your favorite dipping sauce.

ingredients: 2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° Fahrenheit. Line a 9x13” baking pan with parchment paper.
Place the butter and brown sugar in a mixing bowl. Beat with an electric mixer until light and fluffy, 2 to 3 minutes.

Remove the crust from the oven after 15 minutes and pour the cherry sauce on top of the crust, spreading it out evenly.
Place clumps of the remaining crust dough over the top of the cherries and spread evenly across the top.
Place the pan back in the oven and bake for an additional 15 to 20 minutes, or until the crumbles on top are slightly golden brown.
Remove from oven and let cool.
Place the powdered sugar, vanilla, and water in a small bowl and whisk together to form a smooth icing.
Drizzle the icing over the top of the cooled cherry pie bars. Cut into 15 slices.
Store in an airtight container.

product: KODIAK® Buttermilk & Maple Flapjack Power Cup
base: 1 Kodiak Buttermilk & Maple Flapjack Power Cup; 1/4 cup whole milk; 3 tablespoons whole milk ricotta
ingredients: 1 Kodiak Buttermilk & Maple Flapjack Power Cup
instructions: Remove the lid to the Kodiak cup.
Add the milk, ricotta, and lemon zest to the flapjack cup and stir with a fork until combined.
Microwave on high for 90 seconds.
Top with honey and a dollop of ricotta, if desired.
description: This Single-Serve Lemon Ricotta Flapjack Cup is the quick breakfast (or snack) you didn’t know you needed that brings whole grains, 17g protein, and a burst of sweet, creamy citrus to every bite.

name: Single-Serve S’mores Brownie
product: KODIAK® S’mores Flapjack Power Cup
base: 1 Kodiak S’mores Flapjack Power Cup; 2 teaspoons cocoa powder; 3 tablespoons brown sugar
instructions: Remove the lid to the flapjack cup.
Stir in the cocoa powder and brown sugar.
Add the oil and milk and stir until well combined.
Spoon the chocolate hazelnut spread into the center of the batter.
Microwave on high for 60 seconds. Let cool slightly and enjoy!
description: This Single-Serve S’mores Brownie makes a warm, gooey treat packed with classic campfire flavors —chocolate, marshmallow, and that irresistible graham cracker crunch.

name: Brown Sugar Espresso Oat Muffins
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 2 packets Kodiak Maple Brown Sugar Oatmeal Packets; 1/2 cup packed brown sugar
ingredients: 1-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
2 packets Kodiak Maple Brown Sugar Oatmeal Packets

1/3 cup freshly brewed espresso


 

For the crumble topping:
1 packet Kodiak Maple Brown Sugar Oatmeal Packets
2 tablespoons Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375° F. Line a muffin tin with 10 paper liners.
In a mixing bowl, whisk together the Kodiak mix, oatmeal, brown sugar, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt.
Add the avocado, eggs, vanilla, and espresso to the dry ingredients and whisk until a smooth batter is formed. Let rest for 10 minutes (this lets the grains have time to absorb the liquid).

While the batter is resting, make the crumble: add the contents of the oatmeal packet to a small mixing bowl along with the Kodiak mix and brown sugar. Stir to combine. Add the butter and cut in with your fingers until a coarse crumble forms. Set aside.
Stir batter and divide evenly between the liners. They should be 3/4 full. Sprinkle the crumble evenly over the filled muffin cups.
Bake the muffins in the preheated oven for 12-14 minutes, or until golden brown on top.
Cool and store in an airtight container.
description: These Brown Sugar Espresso Oat Muffins combine rich espresso, warm brown sugar, and hearty oats for a bite that’s soft, golden, and packed with flavor.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Sweet Potato Pancakes
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 medium sweet potato, *roasted (about 2/3 cup); 1 cup water; 1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
ingredients: 1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
1/3 cup pecans, toasted (can use candied pecans, if desired)
Butter, to top and grease pan

Maple syrup, to top


 

*To roast the sweet potato, preheat oven to 375° F. Add the sweet potato directly to the rack and cook for 35-40 minutes, or until soft. Remove from oven and let cool in its skin. Use as directed.
instructions: Remove the skin from the sweet potato and discard.
Add the sweet potato, water, Kodiak mix, cinnamon, and vanilla to a blender. Process until a smooth batter is formed.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.

Grease skillet with butter and add a spoonful of batter about 1/4 cup in volume. Quickly smooth into a circle and cook until bubbles form on the top. Flip and cook for an additional 30 seconds, or until golden on both sides.
Repeat the process with remaining batter.
Serve pancakes topped with butter, maple syrup, and a sprinkle of toasted pecans.
description: We've added sweet potatoes to this morning stack for a breakfast of sweet potato pancakes that pack in beta-carotene and antioxidants to every bite. It's a sneaky way to get in some morning veggies don't you think?

name: Dark Chocolate Banana Peel Muffins
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 3 large bananas; 2 flax eggs (can use regular eggs, if desired); 1/3 cup nut butter (peanut, almond, or cashew work well)
ingredients: 2 flax eggs (can use regular eggs, if desired)
1/3 cup nut butter (peanut, almond, or cashew work well)
1-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Peel the bananas and set aside the fruit for another use (freeze for smoothies, use for banana bread, etc.). Wash the banana peel exterior well and place in a heat proof bowl.
Pour boiling water over the banana peels to cover them and let sit for 15 minutes to soften.
Remove banana peels from water and pat dry. Discard stems. Chop the banana peel into coarse chunks.
Place the chopped banana peel in a blender along with the flax eggs, nut butter, honey, coconut oil, and nut milk. Blend at high speed until smooth. Set aside.
Place the Kodiak mix, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a mixing bowl and whisk together. Pour in the banana peel mixture and stir together to form a smooth batter.
Fold in the dark chocolate. Set aside to rest for 5 minutes.
Stir and divide the batter evenly between the liners. They should be almost full. Add additional pieces of chocolate to the top of the filled muffin tins, if desired.
Bake the muffins in the preheated oven for 12-14 minutes, or until golden brown on top.
Cool and store in an airtight container.
description: Kodiak’s Dark Chocolate Banana Peel Muffins turn food scraps into something delicious with whole grains, protein, and rich cocoa. A better-for-you, waste-reducing treat—bake a batch today.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Breakfast Cake
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 2 cups of Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/2 cup brown sugar; 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
ingredients: 2 cups of Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix

1/2 cup chocolate chips, divided 


 

Topping Ideas:
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° Fahrenheit and prepare a 9x13” baking dish with non-stick cooking spray.
In a medium sized mixing bowl, whisk together the Kodiak mix, brown sugar, and cinnamon

Mix in the milk, butter, egg, bananas, vanilla, applesauce, and pumpkin purée. This makes a wet batter, but it should not be runny. If your batter seems too wet, whisk in the remaining flour 1-2 tablespoons at a time until you reach desired consistency
Fold in 1/4 cup chocolate chips. Saving the rest to top the cake
Pour the batter into the prepared baking dish and add the remaining chocolate chips with any other topping combo you desire.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean and the edges of your cake are slightly golden brown.
Let cool for 10-15 minutes in the baking dish before slicing.

Enjoy for breakfast, lunch or dinner! 


 

*Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 5-7 days. Reheat in the microwave for 15-30 seconds before digging in! 

 

*Pro Tip: For even more pumpkin flavor, sub-out Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes for Pumpkin Power Cakes.
description: As a collegiate athlete, Kate W. was always on the hunt for a hearty, protein-packed breakfast to fuel her training. She crafted this Breakfast Cake as an easy, grab-and-go option that turned out to be a hit for her entire...
author: Kate W.

name: Blueberry Protein Pancakes
product: KODIAK® Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1/2 cup reduced fat cottage cheese; 2 eggs; 1 tbsp milk of choice
ingredients: 1/2 cup Kodiak Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Add cottage cheese, eggs, and milk to a blender and blend until smooth.
In a medium-sized bowl, whisk together the Kodiak mix and the blended cottage cheese mixture until well combined.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and grease with butter or oil.
Scoop 1/4 cup of batter for each pancake onto your preheated skillet and allow to cook until puffed and bubbly on top, then flip and continue to cook until golden.
Top your stack with Greek yogurt and a sprinkle of fresh blueberries. Enjoy!
description: These Blueberry Protein Pancakes make a breakfast stack that's ready-to-eat in just 15 minutes with no complicated steps, just simple ingredients that pack in 44g of protein per serving to keep you feeling fuller, longer.

name: Blueberry Flax Muffin
product: KODIAK® Blueberry Muffin Power Cup
base: 1 Kodiak Blueberry Muffin Power Cup; 1/4 teaspoon baking powder; 2 teaspoons ground flaxseed
instructions: Remove the lid to the Kodiak cup.
Add the baking powder and flax. Stir with a fork to combine.
Add the egg, water and avocado oil to the cup and stir to form a smooth batter. Top with fresh or frozen blueberries, if desired.

Microwave on high for 90 seconds. Cool slightly before enjoying!


 

*Note: Muffins can also be baked directly in the paper cup in an oven preheated to 350° F for 12-15 minutes or until puffed and golden on top.
description: This Blueberry Flax Muffin recipe comes packed with nearly 20g of protein per serving. Dig in and see just how full this morning blueberry flax muffin cup will keep you!
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Blueberry Zucchini Bread
product: KODIAK® Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 3 cups Kodiak Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1-1/2 teaspoons baking powder; 1/4 teaspoon baking soda
ingredients: 3 cups Kodiak Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
3 cups shredded zucchini (lay on paper towels to absorb moisture)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° F. Grease and flour two 8x4” loaf pans.
Add the Kodiak mix, baking powder, baking soda, and cinnamon to a large mixing bowl and whisk together. Set aside.
In another bowl, whisk together the oil, egg, brown sugar, granulated sugar, and vanilla.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and whisk together - mixture will be dry.
Add the grated zucchini to the batter and gently fold in. This will loosen up the batter as it absorbs some liquid from the zucchini. Let rest for 5 minutes, then stir again to form a smooth batter.
Divide the batter between the prepared pans. Bake in the preheated oven for 45-50 minutes, or until a tester inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let loaves cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes, then remove from pans and let cool completely.
Store in an airtight container. Will keep longer stored in the refrigerator.
description: Make Blueberry Zucchini Bread with Kodiak baking mix for a moist, protein-packed treat. Fresh blueberries and zucchini combine in this easy recipe. Learn more.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Protein Puff Pastry
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1 cup salted butter, cubed and chilled; 1/2 cup cold water
ingredients: 2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
1 cup salted butter, cubed and chilled
instructions: Add the Kodiak mix to the bowl of a food processor fitted with an ‘S’ blade.
Add 3/4 cup of the butter to the processor and pulse until butter is blended in fully.
Add the remaining 1/4 cup butter and pulse 3-4 times.
Add in the cold water and pulse just until the mixture starts to come together. Tip into a bowl and press together with your hands to form a loose ball. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Place the dough on a lightly floured surface and knead lightly about 10 times.
Lightly flour a rolling pin and roll the dough into a rectangle (about 12” x 18”). Fold the dough like an envelope. Fold in half again.
Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

Use as desired. This recipe will keep in the fridge for 2-3 days or in the freezer for up to a month.


*Note: When baking this specific puff pastry, oven should be heated to 375° F. See our Nutella Puff Pastry recipe. The result of this recipe is not exactly the same as a standard puff pastry recipe because of the lack of gluten.
description: With just two ingredients and a little water, this Protein Puff Pastry comes together in minutes and makes a delicious, whole-grain pastry packed with protein for your next breakfast, lunch, snack, or even dessert.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Nutella Puff Pastry
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 Protein Puff Pastry recipe, thawed and slightly cold; 3/4 cup Nutella; 1 egg, beaten
ingredients: 1 Protein Puff Pastry recipe, thawed and slightly cold
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375° F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Sprinkle a surface lightly with flour and roll the puff pastry into a large rectangle. Sprinkle the top of the pastry with flour as needed when rolling if it seems sticky.
Spread the Nutella evenly over the pastry rectangle.
Cut the pastry into 12 triangles using a pizza cutter or sharp knife.

Starting with the widest end, roll the triangle up to the pointed end and place, end tip down, on the prepared baking sheet. Repeat with remaining triangles until you have 12 crescent shapes spaced evenly on the baking sheet.
Brush the crescents with the egg wash.
Bake in the preheated oven for 13-15 minutes or until puffed and golden brown.
Cool slightly on a wire rack and enjoy warm!
Store in an airtight container for a few days.
description: Sneak in some protein and whole grains as you savor every crisp, buttery bite of the chocolatey greatness that is this Nutella Puff Pastry. It’s wild to know something that tastes this good has the real good stuff in it,...
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Pizza Pinwheels
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 3/4 cup whole milk; 3 tablespoons butter; 2-1/4 teaspoons instant yeast
ingredients: 2-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
1/3 cup pizza sauce (plus extra, for dipping)
instructions: Place the Kodiak mix and salt in a mixing bowl fitted to a stand mixer and set aside.

Place the milk, sugar, and butter in a small saucepan and heat just until the butter starts to melt. Remove from heat, stirring occasionally until butter melts fully and let cool until warm (no longer hot to the touch. Add the yeast and whisk until dissolved.
Pour the milk mixture into the bowl of dry ingredients along with the egg and stir to combine. Beat with a whisk attachment for 5 minutes to form a smooth dough.
Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
Roll the rested dough out into a 14” x 8” rectangle.
Spread the pizza sauce evenly over the dough. Cut the dough into 12 even strips, cutting from short end to short end of the rectangle.
Sprinkle the cheese evenly over the dough strips.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Place 5 pepperoni halves along one dough strip and roll into a pinwheel. Place on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Repeat with the remaining dough until you have 12 pinwheels evenly spaced on the baking sheet.
Cover with a towel and place in a warm area to rise until *doubled in size (45 minutes to an hour).
Preheat the oven to 350° F.
Bake the pinwheels for 12-14 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through.

Serve with extra pizza sauce for dipping!



*Note: Pinwheels do not need to be fully doubled in size to be ready to bake.  A 50% increase in size is enough to bake appropriately.
description: This Pizza Pinwheel recipe is a crafty yet simple way to mix up your pizza routine. Each Pizza Pinwheel makes a fun, and dare we say delicious, way to eat your favorite foods while sticking to your goals.

name: Summer Vegetable Tostada
product: KODIAK® Buttermilk & Vanilla Power Waffles
base: 4 Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Power Waffles; 1 tablespoon olive oil; 1 small zucchini, cut into 1” pieces
ingredients: 1 ear corn, kernels cut from cob
instructions: Place the peas, garlic, cilantro, and the juice of one lime in a food processor. Pulse until blended into a thick paste. Add salt to taste. Pulse again and set aside.

Add the olive oil to a large skillet and heat to medium/high. Add the zucchini, corn, and smoked paprika to the skillet and sauté until golden and soft. Remove from the heat and toss in the cherry tomatoes and green onion. Add salt to taste.
Toast the waffles according to package directions.
Top each waffle with 1/4 cup of the pea mixture and 1/4 of the vegetable mixture. Repeat with remaining waffles.
Serve each waffle tostada with a tablespoon of yogurt and a lime wedge.
description: These Summer Vegetable Tostadas use Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Power Waffles as a crispy, crave-worthy base for all your garden-fresh summer produce. This dish comes together real quick, and will be gone even faster—proving that waffles aren’t just for breakfast...
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Simple Summer Pasta
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 2 eggs; 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil
ingredients: 1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Make the Noodles:
Place the Kodiak mix on a clean work surface and make a well in the center.
Crack the two eggs into the Kodiak mix well and use a fork to slowly blend the egg into the mix.

Once a shaggy dough forms, use your hands to work the mixture into a firm dough ball. Knead the dough ball for five minutes, until smooth and pliable. Cover with plastic wrap and let rest for 20 minutes.

Roll the dough out as thin as you can and use a pizza cutter or knife to cut into 1/8” wide strips. Toss the noodles with a little Kodiak mix so that they don’t stick together. Cover until ready to use.


 

Simple Summer Pasta:
Fill a pot with 6 cups water and a large pinch of salt. Bring to a boil.

While water is coming to a boil, heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium/high heat. Add the cherry tomatoes and sauté until they start to blister, 3-4 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Add salt and pepper to taste. Remove from heat and set aside.
Add the pasta to the boiling water and cook for 3-4 minutes, or until noodles float and are fully cooked.
Drain the pasta and add the noodles to the tomato mixture. Toss with tongs until the pasta is covered evenly in the oil.

Serve the pasta topped with fresh basil and Parmesan cheese.


 

*Note: Fresh noodles should be cooked within 24 hours. Store in the fridge, covered, if not using immediately.
description: This Simple Summer Pasta is delicious proof that your Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes mix can make way more than just breakfast. Dig into a fresh plate of homemade noodles that are surprisingly easy-to-make and seriously satisfying.

name: Single-Serve Chai Muffin
product: KODIAK® Cinnamon Roll Muffin Cup
base: 1 Kodiak Cinnamon Roll Muffin Cup; 1/8 teaspoon ground clove; 1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom
instructions: Remove the lid from the oatmeal cup.
Add the clove, cardamom, ginger, and baking powder to the cup and stir with a fork to combine.
Add the egg, oil, and water to the cup and stir until a smooth batter forms.
Microwave on high for 90 seconds.

If desired, brush top with butter and sprinkle cinnamon sugar over the top.


 

*Note: Muffin can be baked in the oven, instead of the microwave, if desired. Make muffin according to above directions and place cup on a baking sheet or transfer to oven safe dish (like a Ramekin). Bake in an oven preheated to 375° F for 12-15 minutes.
description: Our single-serve chai muffin recipe uses Kodiak Cinnamon Roll Muffin Cup to bring bold flavor to your breakfast in under 2 minutes. Just mix, microwave, and dig into a soft, spiced muffin that hits the spot without slowing you down.

name: Single-Serve Peach Cobbler
product: KODIAK® Buttermilk & Maple Flapjack Cup
base: 1 Kodiak Buttermilk & Maple Flapjack Cup; 1 peach, sliced; 2 tablespoons sugar
instructions: Remove the lid from the Kodiak cup.
Add the melted butter and milk to the flapjack cup and stir to form a thick dough. Set aside.
Place the sliced peaches in a saucepan and add the sugar, cornstarch, and vanilla. Toss with a rubber spatula to combine.
Heat on medium/high and stir occasionally for about 2 minutes, or until peaches have softened and are saucy.

Remove the dough from the flapjack cup. Fill the cup with half of the peaches and top with half of the dough. Top dough with the remaining peaches and spread the remaining dough over the top of the peaches.
Microwave on high for 90 seconds.

Let cool slightly and enjoy.


 

*Note: Cobbler can be baked in the oven, instead of the microwave, if desired. Make cobbler according to above directions and place cup on a baking sheet or in an oven safe dish (like a Ramekin). Bake in an oven preheated to 350° F for 12-13 minutes.

name: Chocolate Raspberry Frozen Yogurt Bars
product: KODIAK® Chocolate Chip Crunchy Granola Bars
base: 1 box (6 packages) Kodiak Chocolate Chip Crunchy Granola Bars; 1/2 cup almond butter; 1 cup fresh raspberries
ingredients: 1 box (6 packages) Kodiak Chocolate Chip Crunchy Granola Bars
instructions: Keeping the Kodiak Crunchy Bars in their packaging, smash each package with a rolling pin to roughly crush up the bars.
Empty each package into a bowl and add the peanut butter. Mix with a rubber spatula until well combined.
Line a 9x9-inch baking pan with parchment paper.
Scoop the granola bar mixture into the lined baking pan and press into a single layer.
Place the raspberries evenly over the top of the granola mixture.
Place the yogurt and maple syrup in a small bowl and whisk until smooth. Pour over the top of the pressed granola and raspberries and smooth evenly.
Place in the freezer for at least four hours or overnight.
Once frozen, lift the parchment out of the pan and the bars sheet on a cutting board. Cut into 10 slices.
Store bars in an airtight container in the freezer.

instructions: Remove the lid from the muffin cup.
Add the baking powder to the cup and stir with a fork to combine.
Add the egg, oil, and water to the cup and stir until a smooth batter forms.
Microwave on high for 90 seconds.

name: White Chocolate Raspberry Cake
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 2-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1 teaspoon baking powder; 1 cup granulated sugar
ingredients: 2-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix

1 cup Raspberries, slightly mashed


 

For the frosting:
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° F. Grease the sides of three 6” round cake pans and line each with parchment paper.
Add the Kodiak mix, baking powder, and sugar to a mixing bowl and whisk to combine.
In another bowl, add the eggs, vanilla, butter, sour cream, and buttermilk and mix until smooth.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and whisk together to form a smooth batter. Fold in the smashed raspberries.
Divide the batter evenly between the prepared cake pans and bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until a tester inserted into the center comes out clean.
Allow the cakes to cool for 10 minutes, then run a knife around the edges and invert each round onto a wire rack to finish cooling.

While the cake layers are cooling, make the frosting: place the white chocolate chips in a microwave safe bowl and pour the heavy cream over the top. Microwave for 45 seconds, remove, and let sit for 30 seconds. Whisk until all of the chocolate melts and a smooth ganache forms. Set aside.

Place the butter and half of the powdered sugar in a mixing bowl. Beat together to form a thick icing. Beat in half of the ganache mixture. Beat in the remaining powdered sugar, then the remaining ganache mixture until a smooth frosting forms.
Frost the cake with the white chocolate frosting, stacking each layer with frosting in between.
Top cake with fresh raspberries.
Store cake in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

product: KODIAK® Honey Whole Wheat Bread (recipe HERE)
base: 2 slices Kodiak Honey Whole Wheat Bread (recipe HERE); 1 tablespoon jam of choice; 1 tablespoon peanut butter
ingredients: 2 slices Kodiak Honey Whole Wheat Bread (recipe HERE)
instructions: Place two slices of bread on a work surface.
Cut a circle out of each slice of bread that is 3-4” in diameter. Discard the crusts or save for another use.
Spread the jam and peanut butter in the center of each circle and sandwich together.
Pinch the circle of dough together firmly around the edges using your fingers.
Seal the edges further by pressing the tines of a fork around the circle.
Store in an airtight container if not using immediately. Best eaten within a few hours of making.

name: Almond Joy Energy Bites
product: KODIAK® Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Protein Balls
base: 12 Medjool dates, pits removed; 2/3 cup almond butter; 2/3 cup shredded coconut, divided
ingredients: 1 box Kodiak Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Protein Balls
instructions: Place the dates, almond butter, and ⅓ cup shredded coconut in the bowl of a food processor. Process until dates are broken down and a chunky paste forms.
Add the protein ball mix and water to the food processor and process until the mixture resembles cookie dough, scraping down the sides as needed.
Let the dough rest for 5 minutes for liquids to absorb.
Roll the mixture into 24 balls, about a heaping tablespoon in volume, each. Roll each ball in the remaining shredded coconut and place on a tray lined with parchment paper.
Place the chocolate chips in a microwave safe bowl and heat at 30 second intervals until melted. Stir until smooth.
Drizzle the melted chocolate over the tops of the protein balls. Let the chocolate set before storing.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
description: These Almond Joy Energy Bites are made with rich almond butter, sweet Medjool dates, and shredded coconut all blended with Kodiak’s Chocolate Chip Protein Ball Mix to make hearty, satisfying, and ready to fuel everything from trail breaks to after-school...

name: Lemon Blueberry Waffle Trifle
product: KODIAK® Buttermilk & Vanilla Power Waffles
base: 4 Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Power Waffles; 14 oz can sweetened condensed milk; 2 cups heavy whipping cream, divided
instructions: Toast the waffles to golden brown and let cool. Cut into bite sized pieces and set aside.

Place the sweetened condensed milk in a mixing bowl and whisk in 1 cup of the heavy whipping cream. Add the lemon juice and lemon zest and whisk - the mixture should begin to thicken quickly. When it has a smooth, pudding-like consistency, set aside.
Place the remaining cup of heavy whipping cream in another bowl with the 2 tablespoons sugar and the vanilla extract. Beat with an electric mixer until it forms stiff peaks.

Layer the waffle pieces, lemon pudding, whipped cream, and fresh blueberries, dividing between 4 individual glass containers (about a cup in volume). You should be able to layer each ingredient 2 times per container.
Top each trifle with blueberries and a sprig of mint.
Serve immediately or cover and store in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
description: This Lemon Blueberry Waffle Trifle is crafted with 100% whole grains (thank you Kodiak waffles) and just the right amount of indulgence for a no-bake recipe perfect for backyard hangs, brunch tables, and everyday cravings.

ingredients: 1 packet Kodiak Maple Brown Sugar Oatmeal Packets

name: Single-Serve Banana Bread Pancakes
product: KODIAK® Chocolate Chip & Maple Flapjack Cup
base: 1 Kodiak Chocolate Chip & Maple Flapjack Cup; 1 small banana (overripe), mashed; 1 tablespoon walnuts, chopped
ingredients: 1 Kodiak Chocolate Chip & Maple Flapjack Cup
instructions: Remove the lid from the flapjack cup.
Add the mashed banana, walnuts, and water to the cup and stir to form a slightly chunky batter.
Let rest for 5 minutes.
Heat a frying pan over medium heat.
Grease, then add the batter - this recipe makes one large or 3 smaller pancakes. Cook batter until bubbles appear on top and the top is no longer glossy.
Flip the pancake(s) and cook for 20-30 seconds on the other side.

Serve topped with butter and maple syrup.


 

*On the run? Cook your pancake right in your Flapjack Cup for approximately 1 minute in the microwave before hitting the road.
description: Give our Chocolate Chip & Maple Flapjack Cup an upgrade with mashed banana and crunchy walnuts for a Single-Serve Banana Bread Pancake that hits like a slice of your favorite quick bread and packs the real good stuff to fuel...
author: Kayley McCabe

name: Lemon Blueberry Bars
product: KODIAK® Blueberry Lemon Muffin Mix
base: 1 Box Kodiak Blueberry Lemon Muffin Mix; 1 cup Kodiak Classic Rolled Oats Canister; 1/2 cup melted butter
ingredients: 1 Box Kodiak Blueberry Lemon Muffin Mix
1 cup Kodiak Classic Rolled Oats Canister

1 teaspoon vanilla extract


 

For the filling:
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F. Line a 9”x13” baking dish with parchment paper.
In a bowl, toss the blueberries with lemon juice, lemon zest, cornstarch, and honey. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the entire box of Kodiak Muffin Mix, Kodiak Rolled Oats, melted butter, honey, and vanilla. Stir until crumbly.
Press about 2/3 of the dough firmly into the bottom of the pan to form a crust.
Spread the blueberry filling evenly over the crust.
Sprinkle the remaining 1/3 dough loosely over the blueberries.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until the top is golden brown and the berries are bubbling at the edges.
Cool completely in the pan before slicing into bars.
description: Bursting with blueberries, tart lemon, and a golden crumble, our Lemon Blueberry Bars recipe is made with 100% whole grains and better-for-you ingredients so you can have your cake and feel good too.
author: Sara Oja

name: Cookie Dough Hummus
product: KODIAK® Crunchy Granola Bars
base: 1 can garbanzo beans rinsed and drained; 1/2 cup almond butter; 1/2 cup real maple syrup
ingredients: 1 can garbanzo beans rinsed and drained
instructions: In a blender or food processor, combine the chickpeas, almond butter, maple syrup, and vanilla extract. Blend until smooth and creamy.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl and stir in the mini chocolate chips.
Enjoy immediately with preferred dippers (we're partial to Chocolate Chip Crunchy Granola Bars 😉), or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.
description: Creamy almond butter, real maple syrup, and a splash of vanilla blend together with garbanzo beans in this Cookie Dough Hummus recipe for a bowl that is smooth, lightly sweet, and seriously satisfying.
author: Sara Oja

name: Neapolitan Waffles
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Chocolate:; 2/3 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/2 cup water
ingredients: 2/3 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix

1 tablespoon honey or maple syrup


 

Vanilla:
3/4 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Preheat your waffle iron to medium-high heat.
In one bowl, combine Kodiak Buttermilk mix and cocoa powder, then add water, coconut oil, and honey. Add to a piping bag and set aside.
In a second bowl, combine Kodiak Buttermilk mix with water, vanilla, and coconut oil. Add to a piping bag and set aside.
In a third bowl, combine Kodiak Buttermilk mix with water, coconut oil, fresh mashed raspberries, honey, and optional beet root powder. Add to a piping bag and set aside.
Prep your waffle iron with non-stick spray, and in the preheated iron, carefully pipe each flavor into 3 equal parts and shut the lid.
Once cooked, repeat step 5 with remaining batter.
Serve warm with your favorite toppings like whipped cream and strawberries. Enjoy!
description: Neapolitan Waffles... they delivers chocolate, vanilla, and raspberry in every bite. So when all three flavors are calling your name, you can answer with "all the above!"
author: Sara Oja

name: Lemon Blueberry Flapjacks
product: KODIAK® Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1/3 cup Kodiak Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/4 cup milk of choice; 1 egg
ingredients: 1/3 cup Kodiak Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: In a medium bowl, mix together the Kodiak mix, milk, egg, Greek yogurt, lemon zest, and lemon juice until smooth.
Gently fold in the blueberries.
Scoop about 1/4 cup of batter onto a greased, preheated skillet.
Cook until bubbles form on the surface, then flip and cook through.
Top with your favorite toppings (we love more yogurt and fresh berries!) and enjoy.
description: This Lemon Blueberry Flapjacks recipe brings together Blueberry Power Cakes, Greek yogurt, lemon, and fresh berries for a stack that clocks in at 34g of protein!
author: Sara Oja

name: Mixed Berry Muffins
product: KODIAK® Blueberry Muffin Mix
base: 1 box Kodiak Blueberry Muffin Mix; 2 eggs; 3/4 cup Greek yogurt
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a muffin tin with paper liners.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, Greek yogurt, milk, maple syrup, and vanilla until smooth.
Add the Kodiak mix and gently stir until just combined.
Fold in the fresh berries gently. If using strawberries, chop them into small pieces first.
Scoop the batter evenly into the prepared muffin tin (12).
Bake for 14-19 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean and the tops are lightly golden.
Let cool for a few minutes before serving.
description: These Mixed Berry Muffins come together in no time with a few simple ingredients for a grab-and-go breakfast that’s protein-packed and seriously satisfying.
author: Sara Oja

name: Pancake Casserole
product: KODIAK® flapjacks
base: 9-12 Kodiak flapjacks, halved; 1/2 cup fresh raspberries; 1-1/2 cup milk of choice
instructions: Make 9-12 Kodiak pancakes as directed on the package. Cut the pancakes into cubes, place them in an oven-safe dish or skillet, and toss in raspberries.
Combine milk, vanilla, eggs, and maple syrup.
Pour the mixture over the pancakes. Cover the dish and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or overnight.
Bake at 350° F for 40-45 minutes.
Serve warm and enjoy!
description: Prep this pancake casserole the night before for big breakfast energy baked to golden perfection come morning.We'll let the family praises for more do the the talkin'.
author: Sara Oja

name: Dark Chocolate Protein Stack
product: KODIAK® Dark Chocolate Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1/3 cup cottage cheese; 2 eggs; 1 tablespoon milk of choice
ingredients: 1/3 cup Kodiak Dark Chocolate Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix

1 teaspoon of maple syrup (optional)


 

Topping Ideas:
instructions: In a blender, combine cottage cheese, eggs, and milk. Blend until smooth.
In a medium bowl, mix the cottage cheese mixture with the Kodiak mix until well combined.
Scoop about a 1/4 cup of batter onto a preheated and greased skillet to make 3 pancakes.
Allow to cook until bubbles form, then flip and finish cooking.
Meanwhile, combine Greek yogurt, peanut butter, and maple syrup in a bowl until smooth.
Layer the flapjacks with the peanut butter yogurt mixture and add desired toppings. Enjoy!
description: With over 30g of protein and 100% whole grains, this Dark Chocolate Protein Stack doesn’t just taste delicious, it’s fuel that’s as bold as it is delicious.
author: Sara Oja

name: Orange Cardamom Pancakes
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom; 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
ingredients: 1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Add all the dry ingredients to a medium-sized bowl and mix.
Add in the wet ingredients and combine to make a smooth batter.
Add 1/4 cup portions to a hot, greased skillet. When bubbles start to form, flip and cook on other side.
Add toppings like honey, pistachios, and yogurt!
description: These Orange Cardamom Pancakes bring 15g of protein per serving to your table, topped with honey, pistachios, and a dollop of yogurt for a touch of sweetness and the perfect crunch.
author: Sara Oja

name: Smoked Gouda & Honey Waffle Bites
product: KODIAK® Buttermilk & Vanilla Power Waffles
base: 5 Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Power Waffles, thawed; 5 slices smoked Gouda cheese; 1 tablespoon honey
ingredients: 5 Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Power Waffles, thawed
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375° F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cut each waffle into four pieces and place on the prepared baking sheet, evenly spaced.
Cut each piece of Gouda into four triangular-shaped pieces.
Top each waffle piece with a triangle of cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven for 5-7 minutes, or until cheese is melted over the tops of the waffles and waffles are toasted.
Remove from the oven and transfer the bites to a serving platter.
Drizzle the bites with the honey, sprinkle evenly with the thyme and red pepper flakes, and serve!
description: Our Buttermilk Waffle Bites with Smoked Gouda & Honey are the appetizer everyone will be reaching for first at your next gathering. This recipe brings protein and whole grains to the table, hidden by wildly delicious flavor that keeps you...
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Glazed Donut Waffles
product: KODIAK® Buttermilk & Vanilla Thick & Fluffy Power Waffles
base: 4 Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Thick & Fluffy Power Waffles; 1 cup powdered sugar; 2-3 tablespoons milk
ingredients: 4 Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Thick & Fluffy Power Waffles
instructions: Place the powdered sugar, vanilla, and 2 tablespoons of milk in a shallow bowl and whisk together to form a smooth glaze. Add more milk if needed to make the glaze thin enough to drizzle off the spoon in ribbons.
Set the glaze aside, covered.
Toast the waffles to golden brown.
While the waffles are still warm, dip one side into the glaze and let the excess glaze drip off into the bowl. Place on a cutting board, glazed side up.
Repeat with the remaining waffles.
Slice each waffle into four pieces and serve.
description: Our Glazed Donut Waffles recipe makes a treat that tastes just like a donut but with whole grains and protein to keep your stomach from grumbling until lunchtime. They’re quick, fun, and perfect for sharing with friends or family.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Single-Serve Maple Pecan Muffin
product: KODIAK® Maple & Brown Sugar Oatmeal Cup
base: 1 Kodiak Maple & Brown Sugar Oatmeal Cup; 2 tablespoons Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes; 1/4 teaspoon baking powder
ingredients: 1 Kodiak Maple & Brown Sugar Oatmeal Cup
1 tablespoon pecans, chopped (reserve a few to top muffin)
instructions: Remove the lid from the oatmeal cup.
Add the power cakes mix and baking powder to the cup and stir with a fork to combine.
Add the egg, oil, and 2 tablespoons of the milk to the cup and stir until a smooth batter forms.
Add the remaining 3 tablespoons of milk  and stir until fully combined. Let sit for 5 minutes.
Stir again and sprinkle the top with chopped pecans. Microwave for 90 seconds.
Let cool slightly. Make maple butter glaze:
Place the melted butter, maple syrup, and powdered sugar in a small bowl and whisk together until a smooth icing forms.
Drizzle the glaze over the top of the muffin and sprinkle with a few pecan pieces. Enjoy!
description: Topped with crunchy pecans and a drizzle of maple butter glaze, this Single-Serve Maple Pecan Muffin makes a cozy bite that works for single-serve pick-me-ups or easy grab-and-go breakfasts on busy mornings.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Pumpkin Oat Energy Bites
product: KODIAK® Chocolate Chip Oatmeal Packets
base: 4 packets Kodiak Chocolate Chip Oatmeal Packets; 1/3 cup Kodiak Pumpkin Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/4 cup chopped pecans
ingredients: 4 packets Kodiak Chocolate Chip Oatmeal Packets
1/3 cup Kodiak Pumpkin Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° F. Coat a mini muffin tin with cooking spray or butter.
Place the contents of the oatmeal packets in a mixing bowl along with the power cakes mix, chopped pecans, and baking powder. Whisk to combine.
Add the maple syrup, eggs, milk, and pumpkin puree to the dry ingredients and whisk together to form a smooth batter. Let sit for 5 minutes to let the grains absorb the liquid.
Stir again and fill each mini muffin tin 7/8 full with batter. This recipe should fill about 36 mini muffin tins. Top each muffin with a pecan half.
Bake in the preheated oven for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown on top and puffed.
Remove and let cool for 10 minutes. Run a butter knife around the edge of each mini muffin and remove from the pan. Store in an airtight container.
description: These Pumpkin Oat Energy Bites pack in whole grains, protein, and a perfect punch of sweet maple flavor. Every bite boasts a hearty combo of oats, rich pumpkin puree, and a satisfying crunch of pecans for fuel that’s both warm...
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Anti-Inflammatory Oatmeal
product: KODIAK® Classic Rolled Oats Canister
base: 1/2 cup Kodiak Classic Rolled Oats Canister; 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon; 1/8 teaspoon turmeric powder
ingredients: 1/2 cup Kodiak Classic Rolled Oats Canister
instructions: Place the oats, cinnamon, turmeric, and ginger in a microwave safe bowl. Stir to combine.
Stir in the water and a microwave on high for 1.5 to 2 minutes.
Top with blueberries, walnuts, chia seed, nut butter, and maple syrup, if desired.
description: This Anti-Inflammatory Oatmeal recipe is proof that simple ingredients can do big things. Ready in minutes, this hearty bowl builds the foundation for your wild side, one spoonful of whole-grain and protein at a time.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Chai Oatmeal Cookies
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 3/4 cup butter (6 tablespoons), softened; 1 cup brown sugar; 1 egg
ingredients: 1-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
1 cup Kodiak Classic Rolled Oats Canister
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the butter and brown sugar in a mixing bowl and beat with an electric mixer until light and fluffy, 2-3 minutes.
Add the egg and vanilla and beat in until combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the power cakes mix, rolled oats, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and beat in until a thick dough forms. Fold in the white chocolate chips
Scoop balls of dough about 3 tablespoons in volume and place 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven for 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown on the edges. Remove and let cool for 5 minutes before moving to a wire rack.

Store in an airtight container.


*Pro Tip: Mix it up by subbing out white chocolate chips for raisins, nuts, etc.
description: Warm cinnamon, cardamom, and ginger spices give this Chai Oatmeal Cookies recipe a chai-inspired kick that's balanced perfectly with sweet white chocolate chips.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Single-Serve Cinnamon Apple Crisp
product: KODIAK® Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal Packets
base: 1 large apple; 1-1/2 tablespoons white sugar; 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
ingredients: 1 packet Kodiak Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal Packets
2 tablespoons butter, cold, cut into cubes
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° F. Coat a small oven safe dish with butter.
Peel and thinly slice the apple.
Place the apple slices in the prepared baking dish and add the sugar and cinnamon. Toss to coat and press apples down slightly.
Place the contents of the oatmeal packet in a small mixing bowl along with the brown sugar. Stir to combine.
Add the butter to the oatmeal mixture and cut in with a pastry blender or your fingertips until the butter is the size of small peas.
Sprinkle the crumble over the top of the apples and bake in the preheated oven for 18-20 minutes, or until apples are soft and crumble is golden brown.
Remove from oven and let cool slightly. Serve with whipped cream or vanilla ice cream.
description: Seeking an excuse to not share your breakfast? Look no further than this Cinnamon Apple Crisp recipe where juicy baked apples and a golden oat crumble come together in one perfectly portioned dish that’s quick to make, and even more...
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Protein Supreme Kodiak Waffle
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 2 eggs; 1/2 cup cottage cheese; 1/4 cup shredded cheddar cheese
ingredients: 3/4 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Preheat and spray waffle iron with avocado or olive oil spray.
Beat eggs in small mixing bowl
Mix in both cheeses and the bacon bits

Stir in the Kodiak mix a little at a time. Depending on the size of your eggs, you may need a little more or less mix (you should be able to pour your batter onto the waffle iron slowly, using a rubber scrapper to clean the bowl).
description: With 26g of protein per serving, this Protein Supreme Kodiak Waffle makes a powerhouse breakfast that keeps you fueled for whatever adventures lay just beyond the breakfast table. Straight from our Community Kitchen, it's too good not to share.
author: Dina Natzel

name: Fiber Loaded Dark Chocolate Cherry Pancakes
product: KODIAK® Community
base: 1/2 crushed Weetabix biscuit (or crushed bran flakes); 3-5 pitted chopped cherries; 1 chopped date
ingredients: 1/2 crushed Weetabix biscuit (or crushed bran flakes)
1/3 cup Dark Chocolate Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Add your pancake mix and crushed fiber cereal of choice (I used 1/2 of a Weetabix biscuit!) to a bowl
Add about 1/4 cup of your liquid. You may need to add more depending on the consistency you want!
Mix in your peanut butter for some healthy fat (totally optional)
Sprinkle and mix in some cinnamon (optional)
Fold in your chopped date and cherries!

Drop about a heaping spoonful onto a heated pan, letting each side cook for 3(ish) and enjoy your delicious pancakes! 


 

*Note: Makes about 4-5 medium sized pancakes. Jessica suggests topping your stack with a drizzle of honey, yogurt, and fresh berries!
description: From our Kodiak Community, Jessica created these Fiber-Loaded Dark Chocolate Cherry Pancakes to kickstart her mornings with something hearty, wholesome, and totally satisfying.
author: Jessica Cochran

name: Leftover Turkey Pot Pie
product: KODIAK® Protein Pie Crust
base: 4 tablespoons butter; 2 carrots, peeled and chopped; 1 potato, peeled and cubed
ingredients: One recipe Kodiak Protein Pie Crust
instructions: Melt the butter over medium high heat in a large pot or Dutch oven.

Add the carrot and sauté for 3 to 4 minutes. Add potato and sauté with the carrots for another 3 to 4 minutes. Add the onion and sauté for another three minutes, or until translucent. At the herbs and sauté for 30 seconds.
Add the flour to the vegetables and stir to coat. Cook for 30 seconds. Add the chicken broth and milk and stir until combined. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Turn off the heat and stir in the turkey meat and frozen peas. Add salt and pepper, to taste. Set aside to cool slightly while you prepare the piecrust.
Preheat the oven to 375° F. Roll half of your pie crust dough out between two sheets of parchment paper in a round to a thickness of ⅛”.
Place the dough in a standard pie dish and smooth to form to the dish.
Spoon the turkey filling into the pie dish.
Roll the other half of the piecrust into a round that is ⅛” thick.
Place the crust round on top of the pie filling and press the edges around the perimeter together. Pinch the edges to seal. Place a few 1” slices at the center of the pie to vent.
Brush the top of the pie crust with the beaten egg.
Bake in preheated oven in the middle rack for 40 to 50 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling inside is bubbling.
Let cool slightly before serving.
description: Our Leftover Turkey Pot Pie recipe proves there’s no such thing as too much turkey. Stuffed with tender turkey, veggies, and a creamy herb sauce, every bite of turkey pot pie is warm, flavorful, and guaranteed to earn a “can...
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Cottage Cheese Toast
product: KODIAK® Buttermilk Power Flapjacks
base:
Kodiak Buttermilk Power Flapjacks; Cottage cheese; Toppings of choice (see ideas below)


 

Toast #1 - Honey Chili Crunch
ingredients:
Toppings of choice (see ideas below)


 

Toast #1 - Honey Chili Crunch

Dash of sesame seeds 


 

Toast #2 - Tomato Basil

Toast #3 - Fig & Pistachio

Top flapjack with 1/4 cup cottage cheese.

Toast #3: Fig & Pistachio: Top the cottage cheese with fig jam and sprinkle with the toasted pistachios.
description: This Cottage Cheese Toast is built on a warm, toasted Kodiak flapjack with endless topping options made for on-the-go, snack attacks, or any time you want something quick, tasty, and totally brag-worthy.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Gingerbread Loaf
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 stick (1/2 cup) butter, room temperature; 1/4 cup packed brown sugar; 1/2 cup molasses
ingredients: 2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° F. Grease and flour the sides of a 9x5” loaf pan (or line with parchment paper).
Place the butter in a large mixing bowl along with the brown sugar. Beat for 30 seconds, until well combined.
Beat in the molasses.
Beat in the eggs, one at a time, thoroughly mixing in after each addition.
Beat in the vanilla.
Add the Kodiak mix, ginger, nutmeg, and cloves to a separate mixing bowl and whisk to combine.
Add 1/2 of the dry ingredients to the bowl of wet ingredients and beat just until combined.
Beat in 1/2 of the buttermilk. Add the remaining flour mixture to the mix and beat in until just combined. Then, beat in the remaining buttermilk just until a smooth batter forms.
Let the batter rest for 5 minutes.
Spoon the batter into the prepared loaf pan, mounding the batter higher in the center.
Bake the loaf in the preheated oven for 45-50 minutes, or until cracked on top and cooked through.
Remove from oven and let cool completely before removing from the pan.
Place the loaf on a wire rack and dust with powdered sugar.
Slice and serve. Store in an airtight container.
description: This Gingerbread Loaf comes out merrily moist and tender, with warm spices that hit in all the right places. Share it with friends, neighbors, or anyone on your nice list, because each slice is filled with a hearty serving of...
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Chocolate Chip Shortbread
product: KODIAK® Chocolate Chip Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 2 sticks (1 cup) butter, room temperature; 1/3 cup confectioners’ sugar; 2 cups Kodiak Chocolate Chip Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
ingredients: 2 cups Kodiak Chocolate Chip Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the butter in a large mixing bowl along with the confectioners’ sugar and almond extract. Beat together until smooth and creamy.
Add the chocolate chip power cakes mix to the butter mixture and beat in to form a very thick dough. Let the dough rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Form the dough into a ball and place on a lightly floured work surface. Roll the dough into a rectangle about ¼” thick.
Cut the rectangle into 12 squares and place them 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake the cookies in the preheated oven for 16-18 minutes, or until just golden brown on the edges. Cool on a wire rack.
Store in an airtight container.
description: These Chocolate Chip Shortbread squares make a buttery, almond flavored, and satisfyingly sweet treat with just the perfect amount of chocolate chips. Enjoy them with coffee, milk, or straight off the rack.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: 3 Ingredient Muffins
product: KODIAK® Blueberry Muffin Mix
base: 1 box Kodiak Blueberry Muffin Mix; 1 5.3 oz container OIKOS Vanilla Triple Zero Yogurt; 1 bottle OIKOS Vanilla Protein Shake
ingredients: 1 5.3 oz container OIKOS Vanilla Triple Zero Yogurt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° F and line a muffin tin with muffin liners.
In a large bowl, mix Kodiak Blueberry Muffin Mix, OIKOS Triple Zero Yogurt, and OIKOS Protein Shake until well combined.
Scoop equal portions of the batter into the prepared muffin tin.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
description: These 3 ingredient muffins pack in 9 grams of protein per serving for an on-the-go option to tackle your everyday adventure. It's wild what you and a Kodiak muffin can do!
author: Sara Oja

name: Maple Pecan Baked Oatmeal Squares
product: KODIAK® Maple Pecan Overnight Oats
base: Oatmeal Squares:; 4 packets Kodiak Maple Pecan Overnight Oats; 1 large egg
ingredients: 4 packets Kodiak Maple Pecan Overnight Oats

4 tablespoons butter, melted   


 

Maple Butter Drizzle:
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° F. Grease an 8x8” or 9x9” baking pan.
Empty the Overnight Oats packets into a mixing bowl.
Add the egg, milk, and melted butter to the bowl and whisk together to form a batter. Let sit for five minutes so that the oats can absorb the liquid a bit.
Transfer the batter to the prepared pan and bake for 15-17 minutes, or until cooked through and golden brown on top.
Let cool completely. Cut into 9 squares.
Place the confectioners’ sugar in a small bowl and add the maple syrup and melted butter. Whisk together to form a smooth glaze.
Whisk in milk, 1 teaspoon at a time until desired consistency is reached.
Drizzle the glaze over the oatmeal squares. Sprinkle the chopped pecans over the top.
Store squares in an airtight container.
description: These Maple Pecan Baked Oatmeal Squares bake up soft, chewy, and lightly sweet with warm maple flavor in every protein-packed bite. This make-ahead breakfast or snack is ready whenever you are for any adventure big or small.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Dark Chocolate Banana Bread Mug Cake
product: KODIAK® Dark Chocolate Sea Salt Overnight Oats
base: 1 packet Kodiak Dark Chocolate Sea Salt Overnight Oats; 1/4 teaspoon baking powder; 1 tablespoon maple syrup
ingredients: 1 packet Kodiak Dark Chocolate Sea Salt Overnight Oats
1 tablespoon oil (avocado, light olive oil, etc)
instructions: Place the contents of the overnight oats packet and the baking powder in a large mug. Whisk together with a fork.
Add the maple syrup, mashed banana, egg, oil, and milk, and stir in with a fork to form a smooth batter. Let sit for five minutes, then stir again.
Sprinkle chocolate chips on top of the batter, if desired.
Microwave the mug for 90 seconds.

Sprinkle the top with coarse sea salt, if desired. Let cool slightly and enjoy!


 

*Pro Tip: Bake your mug cake in an oven preheated to 375° F for 12 to 15 minutes, or until puffed on top and cooked through.
description: This Dark Chocolate Banana Bread Mug Cake is basically a 1-minute answer to every sweet craving—plus a hearty punch of protein. Every bite boasts deep chocolate flavor, a hint of sea salt, and just the right amount of sweetness to...
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Hot-Honey Air Fryer Chicken Bites
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1-pound boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces; 1/2 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/2 teaspoon paprika
ingredients: 1-pound boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
1/2 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Prepare the chicken. Place the chicken pieces in a bowl and pat dry with a paper towel.
Set up the batter station. In one bowl, whisk together the eggs and water. In a second bowl, combine the Kodiak mix, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Coat the chicken. Dip each chicken piece into the egg mixture, then dredge in the dry mixture until fully coated. Set aside.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F for 3 minutes.
Lightly spray the air fryer basket with olive oil. Arrange chicken in a single layer, spray tops lightly, and air fry for 10–12 minutes, shaking halfway through, until golden and cooked through.
While the chicken cooks, stir together the honey, hot sauce, melted butter, and salt in a small bowl.
Toss hot chicken bites with the honey-hot sauce until coated.
description: These Hot Honey Air Fryer Chicken Bites bring the perfect balance of sweet-heat to the table and are a crave-worthy addition to weeknight dinners, game-day snacking, or anytime you’re craving big flavor in a protein-packed bite.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Creamy Chicken & Winter Vegetable Orzo Soup
product: KODIAK® Oat Roux:
base: 2 tablespoons butter; 1 tablespoon olive oil; 1-1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs
ingredients:
1/2 cup heavy cream


 

Kodiak Oat Roux:
1/4 cup Kodiak Classic Rolled Oats Oatmeal Canister, ground into a flour
instructions: Melt the butter and olive oil over medium-high heat in a large pot or Dutch oven.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Add to the pot and sear until golden brown on both sides, about 3–4 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 6–8 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and rosemary and cook for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20–25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Remove the chicken, shred, and return it to the pot.
Stir in the orzo and cook uncovered for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In a small skillet, melt 2 tablespoons butter over medium heat. Whisk in the Kodiak oat flour and cook for 2–3 minutes until lightly golden.
Whisk a ladle of hot soup into the roux, then stir the mixture back into the soup. Simmer 3–5 minutes until thickened.
Reduce heat to low and stir in the heavy cream. Adjust salt and pepper if needed.
Ladle into bowls and serve!

instructions: Add the yogurt, nut milk, chia seeds, and maple syrup to a small mixing bowl. Whisk until smooth and let sit in the refrigerator for 1 hour to thicken.

ingredients:
2 tablespoons Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix


 

Sauce:
1/4 cup freshly grated parmesan, plus more for serving
instructions: Prepare the chicken. Place each chicken breast between parchment or plastic wrap and pound to an even thickness.

Sear the chicken. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear 3–4 minutes per side until golden. Transfer to a plate.
Add remaining oil to skillet. Add onion and sauté 2–3 minutes. Add garlic and sun-dried tomatoes and cook 1 minute.
Sprinkle Kodiak mix over vegetables and stir 30–45 seconds.
Add heavy cream, parmesan, and Italian seasoning. Stir and simmer 1 minute.

Return chicken into sauce, reduce heat, and cook 5–6 minutes until cooked through.

Spoon sauce over chicken and serve immediately.

ingredients: 1/2 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Butter lettuce or romaine, for serving (optional)

Form the mixture into 4–5 evenly sized patties.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Place the patties in the skillet and cook for about 3–4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp.
Transfer the patties to a plate lined with paper towels.

ingredients: 1/2 cup plain or vanilla Greek yogurt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° F.
Place the strawberries, honey, vanilla, and lemon juice in a 9x13” baking dish and toss to combine.

name: Savory Herb & Cottage Cheese Bake
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 box Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1-1/2 teaspoons garlic powder; 1 tablespoon dried oregano
ingredients: 1 box Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
2-1/4 cups Good Culture low-fat cottage cheese, divided
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line a 9 x 13 baking pan with parchment paper or grease.

name: Cookie Butter Cheesecake Cups
product: KODIAK® Cookie Butter Overnight Oats
base: For The Crust:; 2 packets Kodiak Cookie Butter Overnight Oats; 3 tablespoons nut butter(almond, peanut, etc)
ingredients: 2 packets Kodiak Cookie Butter Overnight Oats
8 oz cream cheese(one block), room temperature

1/2 cup heavy whipping cream


 

For The Topping:
instructions: Place the contents of the Overnight Oats packets in a food processor fitted with an “S” blade, along with the nut butter, melted butter, and water.
Process for about 30 seconds or until a thick dough forms.

Divide the dough into eight equal sections and place each section in the well of a muffin tin (preferably silicone). Press the dough in each well against the bottom and sides to form a cup base for the filling.
Chill the cups in the refrigerator for one hour or until firm. While the cups are chilling, make the filling.

Place the cream cheese and sour cream in a mixing bowl and beat with an electric mixer until very smooth and lump free. Add the powdered sugar, cookie butter, and vanilla extract and beat again, scraping down the sides as needed, until smooth.
Add the whipping cream to the mixture, beating in slowly at first, then upping the speed to high. Beat for 20 seconds or until thick, fluffy and smooth.
Remove the oat cups from the muffin tin. Spoon or pipe the filling into the chilled oat cups, dividing evenly between each cup.
Drizzle the cookie butter over the tops of the filled cups and sprinkle each cup with crushed cookies.
Store covered in the refrigerator.

name: Waffle Eggs Benedict
product: KODIAK® Homestyle Power Waffles (frozen)
base:
4 Kodiak Homestyle Power Waffles (frozen); 4 slices deli ham; 4 eggs


 

Simple Hollandaise Sauce:
ingredients:
2 tablespoons butter, melted and warm


 

Topping:
instructions: Toast the Kodiak waffles according to package directions until golden and crisp.
Place the ham slices in a skillet over medium heat. Cook for 1-2 minutes per side until lightly browned around the edges.

Fill a saucepan with a few inches of water and bring to a gentle simmer. Crack each egg into a small bowl and carefully slide into the simmering water. Cook for 3-4 minutes, or until the whites are set and the yolks remain soft. Remove with a slotted spoon.
While the eggs are cooking, prepare the hollandaise sauce. Place the egg yolks, lemon juice, and salt in a blender or small food processor. Blend until smooth.
Slowly drizzle in the warm melted butter while blending until the sauce becomes thick and creamy.
Place two waffles on each plate. Top each waffle with grilled ham, a poached egg, and spoon the hollandaise sauce over the top.
Finish with fresh chives or dill and serve immediately.

instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Place the flatbreads beef-side down onto the hot griddle. Place a ramekin, burger press, or small heavy bowl on top of each flatbread to maintain firm contact with the cooking surface.

name: Waffle Grilled Cheese
product: KODIAK® Buttermilk & Vanilla Power Waffles
base: 2 Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Power Waffles; 1 slice cheddar cheese; 1 slice mozzarella cheese
instructions: Let 2 waffles thaw at room temperature.
Preheat oven or toaster oven to 350°F.
Place waffles on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Top one waffle with a slice of cheddar and the other with mozzarella.
Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until the cheese is melted.
Sandwich together and serve with tomato soup—or enjoy on its own!
description: This waffle grilled cheese packs 24 grams of protein and whole grains into every serving for a comfort food that fuels epic days and wild adventures. Dig in, you'll see!
author: Sara Oja

name: Campfire Baked Apple Oats
product: KODIAK® Maple & Brown Sugar Oatmeal
base: 4 honey crisp apples; 4 packets Kodiak Maple & Brown Sugar Oatmeal; 1/3 cup brown sugar
ingredients: 4 packets Kodiak Maple & Brown Sugar Oatmeal
instructions: Get a steady fire going and let it burn down until you have a nice bed of warm coals for cooking.
In a bowl, combine Kodiak oatmeal, brown sugar, butter, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Carefully hollow out the apples using a spoon. Take your time and be sure not to go all the way through the bottom—this helps keep the juices inside during cooking.
Spoon the prepared filling into each apple. Wrap each one tightly in parchment paper and then in foil, leaving a small opening at the top for venting.
Using tongs, place the wrapped apples in the bed of hot coals. Cook for about 30 minutes, rotating occasionally for even cooking.
Use tongs to carefully remove the apples from the fire. Let them cool for 5–10 minutes. Serve warm with a dollop of whipped cream.
description: The campfire’s hot—and so is your craving for something wildly delicious.These campfire baked apple oats are warm, hearty, and filled with sweet maple–brown sugar flavor in every bite. Kodiak Oats brings the whole grains and protein, Honey crisp apples soften...

name: Gluten-Free Cinnamon Sugar Donuts
product: KODIAK® Gluten-Free Original Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 box (441g) Kodiak Gluten-Free Original Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1-1/2 teaspoons baking powder; 1-1/2 teaspoons ground cinnamon
ingredients: 1 box (441g) Kodiak Gluten-Free Original Flapjack & Waffle Mix
1/2 cup sour cream (or full-fat Greek yogurt)

2 teaspoons vanilla extract


 

Cinnamon Sugar Coating:

2 teaspoons ground cinnamon


 

*Makes 3 dozen mini donuts or 18 standard baked donuts
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F. Grease standard or mini donut pans well.
Whisk together the Kodiak mix, baking powder, cinnamon, salt, and sugar.
In another bowl whisk together the eggs, milk, sour cream, melted butter, and vanilla until smooth.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients just until combined. If the batter is too thick to pipe, stir in 1–3 tablespoons additional milk.
Transfer the batter to a piping bag or large zip-top bag with one corner snipped off. Fill each donut cavity about 3/4 full.
Bake for 11–14 minutes, or until the tops spring back lightly when touched.
Cool in the pan for 3–5 minutes before turning the donuts out onto a wire rack.
Brush the warm donuts with melted butter.
Stir together the cinnamon and sugar and coat each donut generously.
Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for longer storage.
description: It's true, you don’t need to sacrifice taste for your dietary needs, and we made this Gluten-Free Cinnamon Sugar Donut recipe to prove it. These gluten free cinnamon sugar donuts pack in delicious flavor AND real ingredients, so even when...

name: Yogurt Pie
product: KODIAK® Honey Oat Granola
base: 1 cup medjool dates, not packed, pits removed; 1/4 cup boiling water; 1 bag Kodiak Honey Oat Granola
ingredients: 1 cup medjool dates, not packed, pits removed
24 ounces plain Greek yogurt (the thicker the better)
1 cup fresh berries (any assortment - slice strawberries if using)
instructions: Place the dates in a cup and pour the hot water over them. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Measure out 1/4 cup of granola and set aside for garnish.

Place the rest of the contents of the bag of granola. In a food processor. At the soaked dates, reserving any remaining water in the cup. Process for 1-2 minutes or until broken down into small crumbles. Let sit for five minutes so that the granola can absorb some of the moisture.
Process again, adding in as much remaining date water as needed for the mixture to come together in a firm but sticky dough. Dough should hold together easily when pinched.
Press the dough into an even layer covering the bottom sides of a standard pie dish. Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Place the yogurt, maple syrup, and vanilla in a large mixing bowl. Whisk together until smooth.
Spoon the mixture into the granola crust and smooth to level. Top with assorted berries and reserved granola.
Serve in chilled slices. Best eaten the same day made.
description: This no-bake Yogurt Pie features a Kodiak Granola date crust topped with fresh, cool yogurt and crisp, tart berries, that comes together for a wildly delicious, better-for-you treat.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Tropical Protein Pancakes
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1/2 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/4 cup blended cottage cheese; 1 egg
ingredients: 1/2 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix

1 tablespoon unsweetened shredded coconut


 

Pineapple Protein Whip:

1/4 cup very ripe pineapple chunks


 

Topping:
instructions: Place the Kodiak mix in a medium bowl.

Blend the cottage cheese with an immersion blender until completely smooth. Add it to the bowl along with the egg and milk. Stir until just combined, then fold in the shredded coconut. Let the batter rest for 5 minutes.

To make the pineapple protein whip, combine the Greek yogurt and very ripe pineapple chunks in a tall container. Blend with an immersion blender until completely smooth and creamy. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Heat a lightly greased nonstick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Scoop the batter onto the skillet to make 3–4 small pancakes. Cook for 2–3 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through.
Stack the pancakes on a serving plate. Top with generous dollops of the pineapple protein whip.
Arrange the diced mango and pineapple over the top. Sprinkle with the toasted coconut chips and spoon the passion fruit over everything, if using.
Drizzle with maple syrup, if desired. Serve immediately.
description: What do you get when you combine Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes, cottage cheese, and a splash of island flavor? A Tropical Protein Pancakes recipe that packs 37 grams of protein, 10 grams of fiber, and wildly delicious flavor into every...
author: Kayley McCabe

name: Chocolate Coffee Biscotti
product: KODIAK® Chocolate Chip Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 2-1/4 cups Kodiak Chocolate Chip Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder; 1-1/2 teaspoons instant espresso powder
ingredients: 2-1/4 cups Kodiak Chocolate Chip Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
1/2 cup semisweet chocolate, melted for chocolate drizzle
instructions: Preheat the oven to 325° F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the Kodiak mix, cocoa powder, instant espresso powder, baking powder, and salt.

In a separate mixing bowl, beat together the softened butter and 1/3 cup granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes. Beat in the vanilla extract, then beat in the eggs one at a time until fully incorporated.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and mix until a thick dough forms. If the dough seems dry, add 1 tablespoon milk and mix just until combined.
Divide the dough evenly in half. Shape each portion into a log approximately 10-inches long and 3 inches wide with a slightly rounded top.
Place the logs about 4 inches apart on the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 28–32 minutes, or until the tops are set and lightly browned.
Remove from the oven and let cool for 20 minutes.
Using a serrated knife, slice each log into ½-inch-thick slices. Arrange the biscotti cut-side up on the baking sheet.
Return to the oven and bake for 15 minutes. Flip each biscotti over and bake for an additional 15–20 minutes, or until dry and crisp.
Cool completely. Drizzle the melted semisweet chocolate over the biscotti and allow the chocolate to set before serving.
Store in an airtight container for up to one week.
description: Whether you’re serenading your tastebuds at sunrise or getting a quick start to your big day, this Protein Chocolate Coffee Biscotti packs in protein, fiber, and semi-sweet flavor that kicks your motivation into high gear.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Sheet Pan Pancakes
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1-1/2 cups milk; 2 eggs
ingredients: 2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
Top with 1 cup mix of blueberries, blackberries, and strawberries
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper; set aside.
In a large bowl, mix Kodiak mix, eggs, vanilla, and milk until well combined.
Pour the batter onto the prepared baking sheet and top with mixed berries.
Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until set and lightly golden.
Let cool slightly, then slice into 12 slices and serve with maple syrup.
description: This sheet pan pancake recipe comes together in less than 20 minutes, with only 5 ingredients to help make your mornings easy. It's protein-packed and seriously delicious, exactly how breakfast should be.
author: Sara Oja

name: Japanese Cheesecake
product: KODIAK® Cookie Butter Crunchy Granola Bars
base: Kodiak Cookie Butter Crunchy Granola Bars; 1 tablespoon instant coffee; 1/2 cup Greek yogurt
ingredients: Kodiak Cookie Butter Crunchy Granola Bars
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the instant coffee, Greek yogurt, and maple syrup until smooth. Set aside.
Remove one Kodiak Crunchy Bar from the package and crumble it into the bottom of a small dish.
Spoon the coffee yogurt mixture over the crumble and smooth evenly.
Break the second crunchy bar into four equal pieces and gently press them into the yogurt until fully covered.
Microwave the cookie butter for 20–30 seconds, or until melted and pourable. Drizzle evenly over the top.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to set. Enjoy.
description: 5 ingredients is all you need to make this Viral Japanese Cheesecake inspired dish. Each serving brings 24g of protein and crave worthy flavor to the table. Dig in and find out!
author: Sara Oja

name: Blueberry Ricotta Pancakes
product: KODIAK® Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 cup Kodiak Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/2 cup milk of choice; 1/3 cup ricotta
ingredients: 1 cup Kodiak Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Add Kodiak mix, milk, egg, ricotta, and vanilla to a bowl. Mix until combined.
Gently fold in blueberries.
Scoop about a 1/4 cup of batter per pancake onto a heated and greased skillet.
Allow to cook until bubbles form, then flip.
Mix together ricotta and maple syrup until smooth to make a sweet ricotta topping.
Stack and enjoy!
description: This Blueberry Ricotta Pancakes recipe delivers an extra-creamy twist from ricotta, plus plenty of juicy blueberries folded right into the batter. And with 31g of protein, this stack brings a satisfying punch to every serving.

name: Caramelized Banana Granola Yogurt Bowl
product: KODIAK® Honey Oat Granola
base: 3/4 cup Greek Yogurt; 2/3 cup Kodiak Honey Oat Granola; 1 teaspoon coconut oil
ingredients: top with blueberries, maple syrup, and hemp seeds
instructions: Heat a saucepan over medium-high heat. Add coconut oil and allow it to melt, coating the bottom of the pan.
Stir in maple syrup and cook until warm and lightly bubbling. Add the banana slices and cook for 1–2 minutes per side, until lightly golden and warmed through. Remove from heat and set aside.
Assemble the yogurt bowl by adding yogurt to a bowl, then topping with the caramelized bananas and Kodiak Honey Oat Granola.
Finish with blueberries, hemp seeds, and maple syrup. Enjoy!
description: Creamy yogurt, crunchy granola, caramelized bananas, and 36g of protein per serving come together in this satisfying Caramelized Banana Yogurt Bowl. Not bad for something you can throw together before your coffee kicks in.
