name: Chocolate Chip Banana Muffin
product: KODIAK® Chocolate Chip Muffin Cup
base: 1 Kodiak Chocolate Chip Muffin Cup; 1/8 teaspoon ground cinnamon; 1/2 small overripe banana, peeled and mashed
ingredients: 1/2 small overripe banana, peeled and mashed
Chocolate chips to top, if desired
instructions: Remove the lid from the muffin cup.
Add the cinnamon to the cup and stir with a fork to combine.
Add the mashed banana, egg, and milk to the cup and stir until a smooth batter forms. Top with a few chocolate chips, if desired.
Microwave on high for 90 seconds.

Cool slightly and enjoy!


 

*Note: If you prefer to bake your muffin in the oven, preheat your oven to 375° F, place cup on a baking sheet and bake for 12-15 minutes.
description: With 21 grams of protein and just three minutes of prep, this mighty Single-Serve Chocolate Chip Banana Muffin is worth waking up for.

name: 3 Ingredient Cottage Cheese Breadsticks
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base:
1 cup full-fat cottage cheese; 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese; 1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix, plus extra for dusting


 

Topping:
ingredients:
1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix, plus extra for dusting


 

Topping:

1/2 cup shredded Parmesan cheese


 

Garlic Butter:
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375° F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the cottage cheese, shredded mozzarella cheese, and Kodiak mix in a large bowl. Using a pastry cutter, cut the mozzarella into the mixture until a cohesive dough forms.
Divide the dough into 9 equal portions. Lightly dust each portion with additional Kodiak mix and roll into logs about 6-inches long.
Arrange the breadsticks on the prepared baking sheet, leaving approximately 1/4 inch between each breadstick.
Evenly top the breadsticks with 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese and 1/2 cup shredded Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 18–22 minutes, or until the breadsticks are cooked through and the cheese is melted, bubbling, and golden brown.
While the breadsticks bake, stir together the melted butter, chopped garlic, and chopped parsley.

Remove the breadsticks from the oven and immediately brush generously with the garlic butter mixture. Serve warm.


*Serve with marinara sauce for dipping, if desired.
description: This 3-Ingredient Breadsticks recipe brings cottage cheese, mozzarella, and Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes mix together to make soft, cheesy breadsticks with 14 grams of protein per serving.

name: Burrata Bruschetta
product: KODIAK® Homestyle Power Waffles
base: Blistered Tomatoes:; 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved; 4 garlic cloves, lightly smashed
ingredients:
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper


 

Bruschetta:
instructions: Preheat the broiler.
Toss the cherry tomatoes, garlic, and olive oil in a small baking dish. Season with salt and pepper.
Broil for 6–10 minutes, stirring once, until the tomatoes are blistered and the garlic is softened.
Toast the Kodiak Power Waffles until crisp and golden, then cut each waffle in half.
Divide the burrata among the waffle halves.
Spoon the warm blistered tomatoes and garlic over the burrata, then drizzle with the garlic-infused olive oil.
Finish with fresh basil, flaky sea salt, and freshly cracked black pepper. Serve immediately.
description: Crispy Kodiak Homestyle Power Waffles piled high with creamy burrata, fresh basil, flaky sea salt, and cracked black pepper come together in this Burrata Bruschetta recipe that's dishing up 21 grams of protein per serving.

name: Breakfast Brownie Parfait
product: KODIAK® Dark Chocolate Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Fiber Brownies:; 2 cups Kodiak Dark Chocolate Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 3/4 cup granulated sugar
ingredients: 2 cups Kodiak Dark Chocolate Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained

1 teaspoon vanilla extract 


 

Breakfast Brownie Parfaits:
1-2 cups fresh blackberries, raspberries, strawberries, or blueberries, optional
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9 x 9-inch baking pan.
Add the black beans, eggs, melted butter, vegetable oil, milk, and vanilla to a blender. Blend until completely smooth.
Place the Kodiak Dark Chocolate Power Cakes mix and sugar in a large mixing bowl. Whisk together to combine.
Pour the blended black bean mixture into the dry ingredients and whisk until a smooth batter forms.
Spread the batter evenly into the prepared baking pan.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the center is set and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out with a few moist crumbs. Cool completely.
Cut the cooled brownies into 1-inch cubes.
To assemble the parfaits, layer vanilla Greek yogurt, Fiber Brownie cubes, and Kodiak Chocolate Granola in individual glasses or jars.
Repeat the layers as desired and finish with brownie cubes and a sprinkle of granola. 10. Top with fresh berries or other fruit, if desired. Serve immediately.

name: Overnight Lemon Poppy Seed Casserole
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Pancakes:; 2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 2 cups water
ingredients: 2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: For the pancakes:
Combine all ingredients in large bowl and mix well.
Cook pancakes on a hot griddle.
Grease a 9x9" baking pan.

Cut cooked pancakes in half and place vertically in pan.


 

For the custard:
Mix all ingredients together and pour over pancakes.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate several hours or overnight.
Heat oven to 350° F.
Bake casserole 15-20 minutes.
Serve warm with desired toppings.

name: PB & J Muffins
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 cup quick oats; 1/2 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/4 cup powdered peanut butter
ingredients: 1/2 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
1/4 cup coconut sugar, honey, or sweetener of choice
1/4 teaspoon strawberry extract (optional for more berry flavor)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F and line a muffin tin with 6 liners or coat with cooking spray.
Add all dry ingredients to a large bowl and stir.
Add wet ingredients and mix until smooth. Adjust sweeter if desired.
Stir in 1/2 cup chopped strawberries.
Divide and pour into muffin tin.
Add sliced strawberries to the top and drizzle with 1-2 teaspoons of peanut butter.
Bake for 20-25 minutes.
description: Life’s too busy for complicated breakfasts, so we've packed these PB&J Muffins with the good stuff for an on-the-go breakfast that's nutritious, simple, and packed with flavor.

name: Pumpkin Oat Muffins
product: KODIAK® Pumpkin Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 2 cups Kodiak Pumpkin Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/2 cup Kodiak Protein Rolled Oats Canister; 1/2 cup brown sugar
ingredients: 2 cups Kodiak Pumpkin Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
1/2 cup Kodiak Protein Rolled Oats Canister
1/2 cup avocado oil (or other neutral cooking oil)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375° Fahrenheit. Line a 12-cup muffin tin with cupcake liners.

Place the flapjack mix, oats, brown sugar, egg, pumpkin purée, sour cream, milk, and vanilla in a large mixing bowl and whisk together to form a smooth batter. Let sit for five minutes for grains to absorb liquid.
Divide the batter between prepared muffin tins, using a scoop to add about 1/4 cup of batter to each liner.
Top each batter-filled liner with a sprinkling of oats and pepitas.
Bake in the preheated oven for 13-15 minutes, or until lightly golden brown on top.
Remove from the oven and cool on a wire rack. Store in an airtight container.
description: Witches, mortals, and creatures alike are gathering around the patch for one thing this season: Pumpkin Oat Muffins. You can count on protein, whole grains, and the delicious taste of fall in every single pumpkin patch-loving bite.

name: Molasses Cookies
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1/2 cup (8 tablespoons) butter, melted and cooled; 1/4 cup brown sugar, packed; 1/3 cup molasses
ingredients: 1/2 cup (8 tablespoons) butter, melted and cooled
2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.
Combine the butter, brown sugar, and molasses in a mixing bowl. Whisk in the egg to form a smooth mixture.
In another mixing bowl, whisk together the Kodiak mix, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and cloves.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and stir to form a smooth dough (careful not to overmix). Let sit for 10 minutes to allow grains time to absorb liquids.
Divide the dough into 18 pieces and roll into balls. Roll each ball into the granulated sugar and place on the baking sheet, 2 inches apart.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10 to 12 minutes, or until the tops are crinkled and just firm. Cool the cookies completely on wire racks.
Store in an airtight container.
description: Thanks to the Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes, these molasses cookies are not only delicious, but they’re a little heartier too! Soft, chewy, and full of warm spices like ginger, cinnamon, and cloves, this molasses cookies recipe delivers classic flavor with...

name: Single-Serve Blueberry Crisp
product: KODIAK® Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1/2 cup fresh blueberries; 1/2 teaspoon cornstarch; 1 tablespoon honey
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Kodiak Blueberry Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
2 teaspoons butter, cold, cut into small pieces
1 Kodiak Maple Brown Sugar Crunchy Granola Bar, crushed
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375° F. Grease an individual oven-proof dish (about ½-⅔ cup in volume).
Place the blueberries and cornstarch in a small bowl and toss to coat. Add the honey and stir until the blueberries are fully coated. Place in the prepared dish.
Add the Blueberry Power Cake Mix to a small bowl, and cut in the butter with a fork until it resembles small peas. Toss in the crushed Crunchy Granola Bar until combined.
Spoon the crumble mixture over the top of the blueberries.
Place on a baking sheet and bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until blueberries are bubbling and crisp is golden brown on top.
Cool slightly before serving.
description: This Single-Serve Blueberry Crisp features the delicious combination of with Kodiak® Blueberry Power Cakes® and Maple Brown Sugar Crunchy Granola Bars to make a delectable crust with a satisfying crunch to complement it's sweet, and juicy blueberry base.

name: Overnight Biscuits & Gravy Breakfast Casserole
product: KODIAK® Buttermilk & Vanilla Thick & Fluffy Waffles
base: 1 package Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Thick & Fluffy Waffles, defrosted; 16 ounces pork sausage; 1⁄4 cup all-purpose flour
ingredients: 1 package Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Thick & Fluffy Waffles, defrosted
instructions: Place the sausage in a large frying pan over medium high heat. Cook for about 5 minutes, breaking up into pieces as it cooks.
When the sausage crumbles are golden brown, add the flour, onion powder, and 1⁄2 teaspoon salt. Stir in until combined and sautè for an additional 30 seconds.
Add the milk to the sausage mixture and stir every 30 seconds until the mixture comes to a boil and thickens. Remove from heat.
Cut the waffles into 1” thick cubes. Spread evenly over the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish.
Spoon the sausage gravy evenly over the waffles.
Sprinkle the shredded cheese evenly over the gravy.
Add the eggs, cream, pepper, thyme, and 1⁄2 teaspoon salt to a mixing bowl. Whisk until eggs are well beaten.
Pour the egg mixture evenly over the waffle/gravy mixture.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° F. for 30-35 minutes, or until cheese is bubbling.
description: Prep this Overnight Biscuits and Gravy Breakfast Casserole the night before you plan to enjoy it, all you need is 20 minutes! The smell of this breakfast casserole alone will do the work of rounding up the troops for breakfast.

name: Carrot Cake Waffle French Toast Bake
product: KODIAK® Buttermilk & Vanilla Thick and Fluffy Power Waffles
base: 6 Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Thick and Fluffy Power Waffles, thawed; 6 large eggs; 1-1/2 cups whole milk
ingredients: 6 Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Thick and Fluffy Power Waffles, thawed
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Grease a 9x13” baking pan.
Cut each waffle into 4 square pieces. Place them in the greased baking pan, slightly overlapping.
Place the eggs, milk, vanilla, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, salt, cinnamon, and grated carrot in a mixing bowl and whisk together until well combined. Pour evenly over the waffle mixture.
Let sit for 10 minutes. Sprinkle the remaining 2 tablespoons brown sugar and pecans over the top.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown on top.
Cool slightly before serving.
Serve slices of the bake with maple syrup and whipped cream on top.

name: Easy Chicken Parmigiana
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 2 large chicken breasts, cut in half horizontally; 1/2 cup Kodiak® Kernza® Cakes Mix; 1 egg, beaten
ingredients: 2 large chicken breasts, cut in half horizontally
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Place the sliced chicken breasts in the Ziploc bag and pound each breast to about a half inch thick.
Whisk the egg in a small bowl and place in a line with a bowl containing the Kernza cakes mix, and a bowl containing the Italian breadcrumbs mixed with the salt.

Dip one chicken breast in the Kernza cakes mix, turning to coat. Then coat the breast in the beaten egg, shake off the excess and coat in the Italian breadcrumbs, pressing the crumbs into the chicken.
Place the breaded chicken on a parchment lined baking sheet. Repeat the breading process with the remaining three chicken breasts.
Bake the breaded chicken in the preheated oven for 10 minutes.
Remove the sheet of chicken and top each piece with 1/4 cups of marinara sauce, one slice of fresh mozzarella, add 1 tablespoon of shredded Parmesan.
Return to the oven and continue to cook for another 10 to 15 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through, and the cheese is melted and bubbly
Serve with a garnish of fresh basil.
description: Let’s be honest, the best chicken parmigiana in the world is probably found in a quaint little town off the coast in Italy, but it's not as simple as our easy chicken parmigiana recipe.

product: KODIAK® Chocolate Chip Power Waffles
base: 8 Kodiak Chocolate Chip Power Waffles; 2/3 cup plain full-fat Greek yogurt; 1/4 cup peanut butter
instructions: Toast the waffles until lightly golden brown. Layer on a platter.
Place the Greek yogurt, nut butter, and maple syrup in a mixing bowl. Whisk together until smooth.
Spoon dollops of the protein whip over the top of the toasted waffles.
Add banana slices and mini chocolate chips to the top of the waffles.

name: Maple Bacon Donuts
description: Maple is to bacon as these donuts are to you: the ultimate breakfast duo. Our Maple Bacon Donut recipe, featuring Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes, adds the perfect balance of sweet 'n salty taste to a deliciously hearty breakfast you can feel good about grabbing on your way out the door. Each donut is dipped in a rich maple glaze that's complemented by a smoky, salty crunch from crispy bacon crumbles sprinkled on top. Dish up a batch at your next weekend brunch, or prep 'em for the week; either way, there's no denying these maple bacon donuts will make their way onto your regular breakfast menu!
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 3/4 cup whole milk; 3 tablespoons butter; 2-1/4 teaspoons instant yeast; 2-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/4 cup granulated sugar; 1/2 teaspoon salt; 1 egg, room temperature; 1 cup powdered sugar; 1 tablespoon maple syrup; 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract; 1 teaspoon milk; 5 tablespoons cooked bacon, chopped
ingredients: 2-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Place the Kodiak mix, sugar, and salt in a mixing bowl fitted to a stand mixer and set aside.

Place the milk and 3 tablespoons of the butter in a small saucepan and heat just until the butter starts to melt. Remove from heat, stirring occasionally until butter melts fully and let cool until warm (no longer hot to the touch). Add the yeast and whisk until dissolved.
Pour the milk mixture into the bowl of dry ingredients along with the egg and stir to combine. Beat with whisk attachment for 5 minutes, to form a smooth dough.
Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
Place the dough on a floured surface. Roll to a thickness of 3/4 inch. Cut donut shapes out of the dough and place on a parchment lined baking sheet.
Cover the sheet with a cloth or plastic wrap and let donuts rise for about 1 hour or until doubled in size.
Bake donuts at 350 degrees for 11 to 12 minutes, or until cooked through.
Remove from oven and let cool.
Place the powdered sugar, maple syrup, vanilla, and milk in a mixing bowl and whisk until smooth. Add more milk if needed to achieve a thick glaze that drizzles from the whisk in ribbons.
Dip the cooled donuts in the glaze and place on a wire rack. Sprinkle the tops of the donuts with bacon crumbles, about 1/2 tablespoon per donut.
Store in an airtight container.

name: Winter Beef Stew w/ Buttermilk Dumplings
product: Kodiak Cakes
base: recipes
description: Brand-published recipe transcribed from kodiakcakes.com/blogs/recipes/winter-beef-stew (2026-09-15).
instructions: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees Fahrenheit. Add the olive oil to a Dutch oven and heat on high.
Add the beef and cook in the hot oil, stirring occasionally, until meat is browned on all sides.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the frontier cakes mix and toss to coat the beef. Continue to cook for 1 minute, stirring occasionally.
Add the tomato paste and cook an additional 20 seconds. Pour in the red wine and stir, cooking until a thick mixture develops to coat the beef.
Add the carrots, onion, garlic, thyme, and beef broth to the mixture. Stir and bring to a boil. Taste and add salt and pepper as needed.
Once the mixture is boiling, remove from heat. Add a lid (oven proof) and place in the preheated oven. Cook for 1 hour. Once the stew has been cooking for 1 hour, make and add the dumplings:
Place the Kodiak mix in a mixing bowl along with the baking powder, garlic powder, and thyme. Whisk together.
Add the milk and melted butter to the dry ingredients and stir in until just combined. Let the mixture sit for 5 minutes to thicken.
Remove the stew from the oven and carefully remove lid. Spoon the dumpling batter into heaps evenly distributed across the top of the stew.
Replace the lid and place the stew back in the oven. Cook for an additional 10 minutes or until dumplings are cooked through.

Store in an airtight container.

name: Egg Nog Cupcakes
description: For anyone who craves eggnog year 'round... this Eggnog Cupcakes recipe is for you. With help from Kodiak Buttermilk & Honey Power Cakes and everyone's favorite seasonal beverage, we've added this classic holiday flavor not only to the cake, but also to a creamy eggnog-infused frosting. Cinnamon, nutmeg, and a hint of vanilla make each bite feel like you're lounging by a warm fireplace kicking your feet up – does it get cozier than that? Perfect for sharing with friends, family, or anyone who could use a little extra holiday spirit, these cupcakes satisfy all the right seasonal cravings.
product: Buttermilk & Honey Frontier Cakes
base: Cupcakes:; 2-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk & Honey Frontier Waffle Mix; 3/4 teaspoon baking powder; 1-1/2 teaspoons cinnamon; 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg; 6 ounces butter, softened; 1-1/3 cups sugar; 1 tablespoon vanilla; 3 eggs; 1 cup eggnog; Frosting:; 6 ounces butter, softened; 3 cups confectioners sugar; 1/4 cup eggnog; Ground cinnamon, to garnish; Star anise pods, to garnish
ingredients: 2-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk & Honey Frontier Waffle Mix
instructions: Cupcakes: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Line a tin with cupcake liners.
Place the Kodiak mix, baking powder, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a mixing bowl and whisk together. Set aside.
In another mixing bowl, beat together the softened butter and sugar for three minutes, until light and fluffy. Beat in the vanilla. Beat in the eggs one at a time.
Add half of the eggnog and half of the dry ingredients to the mixing bowl and mix until just combined. Add the remaining eggnog and dry ingredients and mix in, again, until just combined.
Let the cupcake batter rest for 10 minutes.
Fill cupcake liners 2/3 full with batter. Bake in the preheated oven for 12-14 minutes, or until just golden brown and cooked through. Remove and let cool completely on a wire rack.
Frosting: Place the softened butter and powdered sugar in a mixing bowl. Add half of the eggnog and beat with an electric mixer until light and fluffy.
Add the remaining eggnog and beat until smooth.
Pipe the frosting on top of the cupcakes. Dust each cupcake with cinnamon and top with a star anise pod.
Store in an airtight container.

name: Pumpkin Pie
description: You're one simple ingredient away from crafting the perfectly delicious and wholesome pie crust — Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes. Surprise your guests with an irresistible dessert that combines our hearty mix with the subtle flavor of creamy pumpkin puree, warm spices, and a touch of sweet maple syrup. Serve with a dollop of whipped cream and a dash of cinnamon for a show-stopping finishing touch.
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Pie Crust:; 2 cups of Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack and Waffle Mix; 1 cup cold, unsalted butter, organic and grass-fed; About 8 tablespoons of ice water; Pie Filling:; 2-3/4 cups pumpkin puree (1-1/2 15-ounce cans yields 2-3/4 cups); 1/4 cup maple syrup; 1/4 cup brown sugar; 1/3 cup unsweetened plain almond milk; 1 tablespoon melted coconut oil; 2-1/2 tablespoons cornstarch or arrowroot powder; 1-3/4 teaspoon pumpkin pie spice (or sub a mix of ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg & cloves); 1/4 teaspoon sea salt
ingredients: 2 cups of Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack and Waffle Mix
1 cup cold, unsalted butter, organic and grass-fed
2-3/4 cups pumpkin puree (1-1/2 15-ounce cans yields 2-3/4 cups)
1-3/4 teaspoon pumpkin pie spice (or sub a mix of ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg & cloves)
instructions: To prepare crust, put Kodiak mix in a large bowl. Cut cold butter into small pieces and add to mix. Then, cut butter into mix using pastry cutter until butter is the size of peas.
Make a well in center of mix and add cold water by tablespoons. Combine just until the dough sticks together and forms a ball.

Divide the dough in half. (After this point you may wrap and chill the dough if you want) Or, on a floured surface, roll dough into a large circle. Place in the pie tin and crimp the edges with your fingers. (Roll dough out onto a floured piece of parchment to make it easier to transport into pie tin.)
For the second pie, repeat with other half of dough, or refrigerate or freeze for another use.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F and prepare pie filling.
Add all pie ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth, scraping down sides as needed. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. Set aside.

If you chose to chill the dough remove from fridge and roll out the crust, unwrap and place it between two sizable layers of wax paper or on a floured surface. Use a rolling pin to gently roll it into the shape of your pie pan.
To transfer the crust, remove the top layer of wax paper and gently lay the pie dish face down on top of the crust and use the support of the wax paper to quickly but carefully invert it.
Place in a pie tin and crimp edges.

Pour filling into pie crust and bake for 58-65 minutes. The crust should be light golden brown and the filling will still be just a bit jiggly and have some cracks on the top. Remove from oven and let cool completely before loosely covering and transferring to the refrigerator to fully set for 4-6 hours, preferably overnight. (If the pie crust begins to brown before filling is done lightly cover pie with tinfoil and continue to cook.)
Slice and serve with coconut whipped cream, whip cream and/or an additional sprinkle of cinnamon, nutmeg, and/or pumpkin pie spice (optional).

name: Caramel Apple Pie
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Crust:; 2-1⁄2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1⁄4 cup shortening; 12 tablespoons (1 1⁄2 sticks) butter, cold and cut into small cubes; 1⁄4 cup of ice water; 1 egg, beaten (optional, used over for crust decor); Filling:; 5 Granny Smith apples, peeled, cored, and sliced; 1⁄2 cup brown sugar, packed; 1 tablespoon cornstarch; 1 teaspoon cinnamon; 1⁄4 teaspoon ground cloves; 1⁄4 teaspoon ground allspice; 2 teaspoons vanilla; 1 cup caramel sauce (jarred); Crumble:; 1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1⁄2 cup brown sugar, packed; 1 teaspoon cinnamon; 1⁄3 cup butter, melted
ingredients: 2-1⁄2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
12 tablespoons (1 1⁄2 sticks) butter, cold and cut into small cubes
1 egg, beaten (optional, used over for crust decor)
5 Granny Smith apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Crust:
Place the Kodiak mix in the food processor bowl fitted with an 's' blade.
Add the shortening to the food processor and pulse once. Add the cubes of butter, one at a time, pulsing a few times after the addition of each cube.

With the processor running, drizzle in the ice water until the mixture starts to form into large clumps. Do not add too much water. Dough should not be sticky or wet, but should come together to form a consistent dough.
Divide the dough in 3⁄4” and 1⁄4” portions. Wrap up the quarter portion and set aside.
Roll the other half of dough into a ball and place it between two sheets of parchment paper. Roll to a circle that is 1.5-2” larger in circumference than your pie dish.

Place the sheet of dough over the top of your pie dish and remove parchment paper. Press the dough in to fit the bottom and sides of the dish. There should be a little bit of dough left hanging over the edges. Trim dough so that it evenly hangs over the edge about 1⁄2”.
Cut the dough about 1⁄2” in from the rim.
Set aside and make the pie filling.
Filling:

Add the sliced apples, brown sugar, cornstarch, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, and vanilla to a large bowl and toss together until the apples are coated. Add the caramel sauce and toss until well distributed.
Spoon the filling into the dough-filled pie dish and pack down so there are no large spaces between apple slices.
Set aside.
Crumble:
Preheat the oven to 375 °F.
Place the Kodiak mix, brown sugar, and cinnamon in a small bowl and whisk together with a fork. Pour in the melted butter and mix in with the fork until the mixture clumps together.
Sprinkle the crumbles evenly over the top of the apples.
If desired, use the pie crust dough that was set aside to roll out and cut shapes to place around the edge of the crust. Brush crust with an egg wash.
Place a tin foil tent over the top of the pie.
Bake in the preheated oven for 45 minutes. Remove the tin foil and bake for an additional 15-20 minutes, or until the filling is bubbling.
Remove and let cool. Serve warm with additional caramel sauce, if desired.

ingredients: 2-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
12 tablespoons (1-1/2 sticks) butter, cold and cut into small cubes
2 tablespoons Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Mix
instructions: Crust: Place the Kodiak mix in the food processor bowl fitted with an 's' blade.
Add the shortening to the food processor and pulse once. Add the cubes of butter, one at a time, pulsing a few times after the addition of each cube.

With the processor running, drizzle in the ice water until the mixture starts to form into large clumps. Do not add too much water. Dough should not be sticky or wet, but should come together to form a nice dough.
Divide the dough in half, wrap up one half and set aside.
Roll the other half of dough into a ball and place it between two sheets of parchment paper. Roll to a circle that is 1-1/2 to 2 inches larger in circumference than your pie dish.

Place the sheet of dough over the top of your pie dish and remove parchment paper. Press the dough in to fit the bottom and sides of the dish. There should be a little bit of dough left hanging over the edges. Trim dough so that it evenly hangs over the edge about 1/2 inch.
Cut the dough about 1/2 inch in from the rim.
Prick the dough all over with a fork. Line with parchment paper and fill with pie weights or beans.
Par-bake in an oven preheated to 375 degrees F for 10 minutes. Remove from the oven and take out the parchment and pie weights.
Set aside and make the pie filling.
Filling: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
Place the sugar, brown sugar, corn syrup, butter, eggs, vanilla, Kodiak mix, and salt in a large bowl and whisk together until the mixture is smooth.
Fold the pecan halves into the mixture.
Pour the mixture into the par-baked pie crust.
Roll out the remaining dough and cut out small shapes with a cookie cutter.
Brush the beaten egg along the rim of the pie and place the shapes all along the rim. Brush the dough shapes with the beaten egg.
Tent the pie with tin foil.
Bake the pie in the preheated oven for 15 minutes, then reduce the heat to 350 degrees F.
Bake for an additional 40 minutes, removing the tin foil tent after 30 minutes.
Remove and cool to room temperature before serving.

instructions: Place acai berry packet, milk, frozen banana, and frozen berries into a blender and blend until smooth.
Empty the smoothie in a bowl and top with Kodiak Crunchy Bar, banana, berries, shredded coconut, and chia seeds
author: Sara Oja

name: Air Fryer Chicken And Waffles
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1-pound fresh chicken tenders; 1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/2 teaspoon salt; 1/2 teaspoon black pepper; 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika; 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder; 1/2 teaspoon onion powder; 1 large egg; 1 tablespoon olive oil; 6 Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Thick and Fluffy Power Waffles; 3 tablespoons butter, cut into three pieces; 6 tablespoons Maple syrup
ingredients: 1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
6 Kodiak Buttermilk & Vanilla Thick and Fluffy Power Waffles
3 tablespoons butter, cut into three pieces
description: Why reserve the indulgence of a classic Chicken and Waffles meal for the weekend? This beloved sweet and savory duo is now an everyday possibility, thanks to a few kitchen shortcuts.
instructions: Place the Kodiak Power Cakes mix, salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder in a shallow bowl and stir to combine well.
Place the egg in a shallow bowl and beat well.
Pat the chicken tenders dry with a paper towel.
Working one tender at a time, coat with flour mixture, dip in the beaten egg, and place back in the flour mixture to coat. Place on a plate and repeat with the remaining chicken tenders.
Heat an air fryer to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
Drizzle the breaded chicken tenders with the olive oil and place in the air fryer basket. Fry for 6-8 minutes or until a thermometer inserted in the center of a tender reads 165° Fahrenheit.
While the chicken is cooking, toast the waffles in a toaster until golden brown.
Serve the toasted waffles warm topped with a pat of butter, chicken tenders and a drizzle of maple syrup (~2 waffles + ⅓ of the chicken tenders, 1 tablespoon butter, and 2 tablespoons maple syrup).
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Air Fryer Oats
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 cup Kodiak Power Oats Oatmeal Canister; 2 teaspoons pumpkin pie spice; 1 teaspoon baking powder; 1/4 teaspoon salt; 1 egg; 1/2 cup milk; 1/2 cup pumpkin puree; 1/4 cup maple syrup; 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract; 1/4 cup pecans
ingredients: 1 cup Kodiak Power Oats Oatmeal Canister
description: When fall rolls around, the seasonal basics come out of the woodwork—cue pumpkin spice everything. And although pumpkin ingredients stand out in Air Fryer Oatmeal, this recipe is far from basic.
instructions: Grease a 6” cake pan; set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk the Kodiak Power Oats, pumpkin pie spice, baking powder, and salt until combined.
Whisk in the egg, milk, pumpkin puree, maple syrup, and vanilla.
Transfer oatmeal mixture to the greased cake pan.
Bake in an air fryer at 330°F for 15-20 minutes.
author: Sara Drury

name: Almond Butter Banana Bars
product: KODIAK® Chocolate Chip Crunchy Granola Bars
base: 1 pack Kodiak Chocolate Chip Crunchy Granola Bars; 1 tablespoon almond butter; 1 banana; Nuts and seeds of choice (optional)
ingredients: 1 pack Kodiak Chocolate Chip Crunchy Granola Bars
description: Kodiak’s Almond Butter & Banana Bars combine hearty whole grains, real banana, and creamy almond butter for a nourishing, better-for-you snack that’s easy to make and ready to enjoy—bake now.
instructions: Remove crunchy bars from packaging.
Spread 1/2 tablespoon almond butter on each bar.
Cut the banana into slices and lay over the almond butter.
Top with nuts and seeds if desired.
author: Sara Oja

name: Apple Brown Sugar Power Waffles
product: Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 large apple; 4 tablespoons salted butter; 1/4 cup brown sugar; 1 tablespoon water; 1 cup Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 3/4 cup whole milk (or water)*; 1 tablespoon oil; 1 egg (optional)
ingredients: 1 cup Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
description: Our Apple Brown Sugar Waffles recipe makes a drool-worthy breakfast packed with protein and 100% whole grains all topped off with sweet fruit and sugary goodness.
instructions: Peel and core the Apple. Cut into half-inch cubes.
Melt the butter in a heated skillet. Add cubed apples and sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add the brown sugar to the skillet with the apples and stir in until dissolved. Simmer for two minutes, until thickened.
Add water and simmer for another 30 seconds.
Remove from heat.
Preheat and grease a waffle iron.
Whisk together Kodiak mix, milk, oil, and optional egg in a mixing bowl until just combined—careful not to over mix. Let rest for a few minutes while the waffle iron heats up.
Spoon about 1/3 cup of batter into each waffle grate and cook until golden brown, about 1-1/2 minutes. Repeat until all waffle batter has been cooked.
Stack waffles and serve warm with the brown sugar apple mixture. Enjoy!
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Apple Bundt Cake
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Cake:; 3 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon; 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg; 3 eggs; 1 cup oil; 1 cup brown sugar; 3/4 cup sour cream; 1/2 cup milk; 1 tablespoon vanilla extract; 3 cups apples, peeled and diced; Icing:; 1/2 cup brown sugar; 1/4 cup unsalted butter; 1/4 cup heavy cream; 1 teaspoon vanilla extract; 1/2 cup powdered sugar
ingredients: 3 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
description: This Apple Bundt Cake recipe combines crisp apple flavor with Kodiak’s whole grain mix for a better-for-you dessert that’s hearty, delicious, and packed with protein. Bake your slice of comfort—get started now.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F.
In a large bowl, combine the Kodiak mix, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs, oil, brown sugar, sour cream, milk, and vanilla.
Whisk the wet ingredients into the dry until the batter is fully combined, and no lumps remain.
Fold the diced apples into the batter.

Use a pastry brush to coat the Bundt pan with melted shortening or oil. For extra protection against sticking, sprinkle a light coating of almond flour or granulated sugar on the pan (be sure to complete this step right before baking. Any earlier could cause sticking to occur).
Pour batter into the greased pan.
Bake for 40-45 minutes or until a toothpick into the center comes out clean.
Let cool for 10 minutes.
Use a table knife to loosen up the sides of the cake from the pan. Then, flip the cake out of the pan and onto a cooling rack. Let cool completely.
To make the icing, combine the brown sugar, butter, and heavy cream or milk in a medium saucepan.
Heat the mixture over medium heat, bringing it to a boil for one minute, while whisking constantly.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla.
Whisk in the powdered sugar, a little at a time, until full incorporated and smooth. Continue to stir until the icing thickens but remains pourable.
Pour the glaze over cooled cake. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
author: Sara Oja

name: Apple Butter Pancakes
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 2 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1 egg; 1-1/2 cup water; 1/2 cup apple butter
ingredients: 2 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
description: Our Kodiak apple butter pancakes recipe is a must try! It only has four ingredients and makes a tasty, healthy breakfast. Try our apple butter pancakes recipe!
instructions: In a large bowl, mix all ingredients together.
Cook pancakes on a large, greased cast iron skillet over medium heat.
Top with apple butter and serve while pancakes are still hot!
author: Sara Drury

name: Apple Cider Donuts
description: Get ready to cozy up with our Apple Cider Donuts—a staple fall favorite treat made better with help from Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes. These donuts are a match made in heaven for those crisp autumn days that pair deliciously with a steaming, comforting mug of cider. Even better? Each donut packs in 100% whole grains, turning this indulgent treat into a satiating, better-for-you breakfast or snack. Share them with friends and family or keep them all to yourself (we won't tell!)
product: Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Donuts:; 1-1/2 cup Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle mix; 1/4 cup brown sugar; 1 teaspoon baking powder; 1/2 cup apple cider; 1 teaspoon vanilla extract; 1 egg; 1/4 cup coconut oil, melted; Glaze:; 1 cup powdered sugar; 1/2 teaspoon vanilla; 2 tablespoons apple cider
ingredients: 1-1/2 cup Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle mix
instructions: In a bowl, combine Kodiak mix, brown sugar, and baking powder and mix.
Add apple cider, egg, vanilla extract, and melted coconut oil.
Mix until just combined.
Divide batter into greased donut pans and bake at 350 for 12-15 minutes or until toothpick comes clean.
Let donuts cool while you make the glaze.
In a small bowl, combine powdered sugar, vanilla and apple cider.
Mix until smooth.
Drizzle glaze over cooled donuts and serve.

name: Apple Cinnamon Compote Pancakes
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 cup Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 3/4 cup water, or milk; 4 tablespoons of Butter; One large apple, chopped; 1 teaspoon cinnamon; 1/2 cup sugar, or sugar replacement; ~ 1 cup Greek yogurt; ~ 4 tablespoons maple syrup
ingredients: 1 cup Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
description: There’s something special about breakfast that brings everyone to the table — and for Kodiak Community member Paulina, these Apple Cinnamon Compote Pancakes do just that. Each stack packs 14g of protein per serving and a hearty, wholesome flavor you...
instructions: In a medium-sized mixing bowl, combine the Kodiak mix and water to make a smooth batter.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the apples, cinnamon, and sugar, and cook until the apples are tender. Set aside. (Pro tip: make extra ahead of time to have all week!)
Cook pancakes per the package instructions. Top them with a dollop of Greek Yogurt, apple compote, and drizzle with maple syrup. Enjoy!
author: Paulina Tovar

name: Apple Cinnamon Flapjack Bake
product: Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Apple Topping:; 2 tablespoons butter; 4 large granny smith apples, peeled and sliced; 1/3 cup water; 1 tablespoon cornstarch; 1/4 cup brown sugar; 1 teaspoon cinnamon; Cinnamon Flapjack Bake:; 4 eggs; 1 cup Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 3/4 cup milk; 1 tablespoon butter
ingredients: 4 large granny smith apples, peeled and sliced
1 cup Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Flapjack & Waffle Mix
description: Kodiak’s Apple-Cinnamon Flapjack Bake is a hearty, oven-baked breakfast made with 100% whole grains, real apples, and warm spices for a better-for-you start to your day. Try the recipe now.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400° F.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the peeled and sliced apples to the pan and cook for 2-3 minutes or until apples soften.
In a small bowl, stir the water and cornstarch together.

Add the cornstarch mixture, brown sugar, and cinnamon to the apples; stir. Cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and the apples are tender. Turn the heat to low to keep warm.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until lightly beaten.
Add the Kodiak Cakes mix and milk to the eggs. Stir until fully combined.
Place the butter in a shallow 10-12 inch cast iron skillet and heat in the oven until butter is melted and the pan is hot.
Remove from the oven and swirl the butter around to coat the bottom of the pan.
Pour the flapjack batter into the hot pan and place back in the oven to bake for 10-15 minutes or until a toothpick into the center comes out clean.
Top the flapjack bake with the cooked apples.
Serve warm with maple syrup.
author: Sara Oja

name: Apple Cinnamon Oat Pecan Sheet Pan Flapjack
product: Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Sheet Pan Flapjack:; 2 cups Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1 tablespoon brown sugar; 1 teaspoon vanilla extract; 2 cups milk; 2 large eggs; 2 tablespoons melted butter; 1/2 cup toasted pecans; Toppings:; 1 tablespoon brown sugar; 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon; 1 tablespoon oats; 2 apples, sliced; Maple syrup to serve
ingredients: 2 cups Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
description: Apple Cinnamon Sheet Pan Flapjacks — the perfect solution for when you’ve got a crowd to feed or just a grizzly-sized appetite (usually the case 😉).
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 F. Coat a 9x13” pan with butter or non-stick cooking spray.
In a medium bowl, whisk together Kodiak mix, brown sugar, and pecans.
In a separate medium bowl, whisk together milk, eggs, vanilla and melted butter.
Whisk the wet and dry ingredients together gently until just combined. Pour into the prepared baking sheet and spread batter to the outer edges of the pan.
Core and thinly slice apples and arrange on top of the batter.
Mix the brown sugar, oats, and cinnamon together and sprinkle over the flapjack batter.
Bake for 18-22 minutes or until edges are golden brown and the top springs back to a light touch.
Serve warm with additional butter and maple syrup as desired.
author: Moments of Mild

name: Apple Cinnamon Rolls
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 3/4 cup + 2 tablespoons whole milk; 8 tablespoons butter, divided; 2-1/4 teaspoons instant yeast; 2-1/4 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1 packet Kodiak Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal Packets; 1/4 cup granulated sugar; 1/2 teaspoon salt; 1 egg, room temperature; 1/3 cup brown sugar, packed; 1 tablespoon cinnamon; 1 large apple, peeled and diced into small pieces; 4 ounces cream cheese, softened; 2/3 cup powdered sugar; 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon; 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
ingredients: 2-1/4 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
1 packet Kodiak Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal Packets
1 large apple, peeled and diced into small pieces
description: This Apple Cinnamon Rolls recipe bring all the cozy fall flavors to your table with a boost of whole grains and protein. Each Apple Cinnamon Roll bakes up soft, fluffy, and ready to keep you going through all the wild...
instructions: Place the power cakes mix, contents of the oatmeal packet. sugar, and salt in a mixing bowl fitted to a stand mixer and set aside.

Place the milk and 3 tablespoons of the butter in a small saucepan and heat just until the butter starts to melt. Remove from heat, stirring occasionally until butter melts fully and let cool until warm (no longer hot to the touch). Add the yeast and whisk until dissolved.
Pour the milk mixture into the bowl of dry ingredients, add the egg, and stir to combine. Beat with the whisk attachment for 5 minutes, to form a smooth, somewhat sticky dough.
Cover and let rest for 10 minutes while you make the filling.
Place 3 tablespoons of softened butter, the brown sugar, and the cinnamon in a small bowl. Stir until a smooth mixture forms. Set aside.
Dust your work surface with flour and press or roll the rested dough out into a 14” x 8” rectangle.

Spread the filling evenly over the dough. Sprinkle the chopped apple pieces evenly over the cinnamon filling. Roll the dough into a 14” long log. Use floss or a sharp knife to cut the log into 10 cinnamon rolls.
Place the cinnamon rolls in a greased 8-9” skillet. Cover and let rise until almost doubled in size.
Preheat the oven to 350° F. Bake the rolls for 23-25 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through.

While the rolls are cooking, make the icing. Place the last 2 tablespoons of butter in a mixing bowl along with the cream cheese, vanilla, cinnamon, and powdered sugar. Beat until a smooth icing is formed.
Spread the icing over the top of the cinnamon rolls once cooled. Store in an airtight container.
author: Kitchen McCabe

name: Apple Cranberry Crumble
product: Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Filling:; 2 cups Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjacks and Waffle mix; 1-1/2 cups water; 2 granny smith apples, peeled and sliced; 1/2 cup fresh or frozen cranberries; 1/3 cup brown sugar; Crisp:; 1 cup Kodiak Rolled Oats Canister; 1/4 cup Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack and Waffle mix; 1/4 cup brown sugar; 1 teaspoon cinnamon; 6 tablespoon butter, cold and cubed; Powdered sugar for topping
ingredients: 2 cups Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjacks and Waffle mix
2 granny smith apples, peeled and sliced
1/4 cup Kodiak Cinnamon Oat Power Cakes Flapjack and Waffle mix
description: Kodiak’s Apple Cranberry Crumble blends tart cranberries, crisp apples, and a golden whole grain topping into a warm, protein-packed dessert that’s easy to make and even easier to love—bake it today.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F
In a large bowl, stir the Kodiak mix and water together until batter is combined
Pour 1/4 cup of batter onto a heated and greased pan or griddle. Cook on medium-high heat until bubbles form on the top. Flip and continue to cook until golden brown
Cut the pancakes into cubes and mix with the sliced apples, cranberries, and brown sugar. Place the mixture in a greased 9" x 13" baking dish
In a medium bowl. Combine the rolled oats, Kodiak mix, brown sugar, and cinnamon
Add the cold, cubed butter and use your fingers to rub it into the oat mixture until crumbly
Place the crumbles over the top of the filling
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until the filling is juicy and the top is browned
Sprinkle with powdered sugar and serve warm
author: Sara Oja

name: Apple Fritter Bread
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Bread:; 1-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes; 2 teaspoons baking powder; 1/2 teaspoon salt; 1/2 cup butter; 1/2 cup sugar; 2 eggs; 1 tablespoon vanilla extract; 1/2 cup milk; Apple Filling:; 2 cups granny smith apples, peeled and chopped; 1 tablespoon sugar; 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon; Topping:; 1/4 cup brown sugar; 1 teaspoon cinnamon
ingredients: 2 cups granny smith apples, peeled and chopped
description: Fall in love all over again with a homemade loaf of fresh baked Apple Fritter Bread. Although apples are fresh for the pickin’ in the fall, you can find ripe ones at your local market year-round. Thank heavens for that—because...
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F and grease a loaf pan with oil or butter.
In a medium bowl, combine the Kodiak mix, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, use an electric mixer to cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, followed by the vanilla extract.
Add half of the flour mixture and mix on low speed. Then, mix in the milk. Add the remaining flour and mix until flour is combined, being careful not to over mix.
Add half of the batter into the loaf pan.
Make the filling by combining the chopped apples with the sugar and ground cinnamon.
Add the apple filling over the top of the batter in the pan. Spread the remaining batter evenly over the apples.
In a small bowl, combine the brown sugar and cinnamon together. Sprinkle the cinnamon sugar over the top of the batter.
Bake the bread for 50-60 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cool before slicing. Store in a sealed container for up to 7 days.
author: Sara Drury

name: Apple Pie
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: Pie dough:; 2-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/2 teaspoons salt; 1 cup (2 sticks) butter, cold; 1/2 cup ice water; 1 tablespoon vinegar; Filling:; 8 granny smith apples, peeled and sliced; 1/3 cup granulated sugar; 1/4 cup brown sugar; 1 tablespoon lemon juice; 1/4 cup flour; 1 teaspoon vanilla extract; 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon; 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg; Other:; 1 egg white; 1 egg; A pinch of salt; 1-2 teaspoons coarse sugar for topping
ingredients: 2-1/2 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
8 granny smith apples, peeled and sliced
instructions: In a large bowl, combine Kodiak mix and salt.
Work the cold, cubed butter into the mix by hand or using a pastry cutter until crumbly.
Mix in ice water and vinegar until a dough is formed. If the mixture is crumbly, add 1 tbsp. water at a time only until the dough comes together.
Divide the dough into two pieces and flatten into discs. Wrap in plastic and refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
Meanwhile, combine the apples, granulated sugar, brown sugar, lemon juice, flour, vanilla, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
On a floured surface, roll one disc of dough about 1/8-inch to 1/4-inch thick.
Transfer the dough into a 9-inch pie pan and brush the bottom of the dough with egg white to create a barrier between the crust and the fruit filling.
Fill with apple mixture.
Roll out the second disc of pie dough and cut into about twelve 1-inch strips. For thin strips, cut the 1-inch strips in half.
Form the lattice by arranging half of the strips horizontally across the pie. Place the remaining strips vertically while threading under and over every other horizontal strip.
Use scissors to cut all except 1-inch of excess dough from the rim of the pan.
Fold the extra dough under itself at the rim to form a crust and press with a fork or crimp.
(Optional) Use leaf pie-cutters to create shapes out of the excess dough to decorate the top of the pie.
Freeze the pie for 15-20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 425° F.
Crack the egg into a small bowl, add a pinch of salt, and whisk to break up the yolk and the white.
Brush the egg over the pie dough and sprinkle lightly with coarse sugar.
Bake the pie at 425° F for 20 minutes.
Reduce the temperature to 350° F and continue to bake for 40-45 minutes or until the apple filling begins to bubble and the crust is golden.

name: Apple Stack Cake
description: Whether you're hosting an autumn gathering or simply craving something sweet and tart to kick off the season, this Apple Butter Stack Cake delivers big flavor. Made using Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix helps pack in 100% whole grains and protein to keep you feeling full and satisfied throughout your fall adventures. Each layer is slathered with a richly spiced salted apple butter that brings out that perfect balance between sweet and savory taste. Dig in, and find out just how dang irresistible this warm cinnamon and apple flavored dessert can be!
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 4 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon; 3/4 cup unsalted butter, softened; 1-1/2 cup sugar; 2 eggs; 2 teaspoons vanilla; 1/2 cup buttermilk; 2-1/2 cups apple butter
ingredients: 4 cups Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F and trim 8-9 inch circles out of parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix and cinnamon; set aside.
In a separate large bowl, use an electric mixer to beat the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy.
Add the eggs one at a time. Then, mix in vanilla.
Add the dry mixture alternatively with the buttermilk, making sure to begin and end with the dry.
Evenly divide the dough into 8 pieces and form each into a disk in the center of the parchment circles.
Dust the top of each disk with Kodiak mix or flour and use a rolling pin to roll the dough out to the edges of each parchment circle.
Transfer the parchment circles with the rolled-out dough onto a sheet pan.
Bake for 10-12 minutes or until the edges are lightly browned. Repeat with remaining dough until all layers are baked.
Once all the layers have cooled, assemble the cake by spreading 1/3 cup of apple butter between each layer. Dust the top layer with powdered sugar.
Cover and refrigerate for 24 hours before serving. (Refrigerating for 24 hours before serving will allow the cake to moisten and become easier to slice.)

name: Apple Stuffed Kodiak Blueberry Muffins
description: Apple-stuffed blueberry muffins — slow roasted over an open fire 🤤. It's only natural to salivate over this dish, as many of the ingredients come from nature. When in the wild, amiright? Take a scrumptious box of Kodiak Blueberry Muffin mix, Mountain Berry Syrup, and a few other essentials to cook a delicious, hearty dish you'll be thinking about the whole hike home.
product: KODIAK® Blueberry Muffin Mix
base: To Make:; 4 granny smith apples; zest of 1 lemon; 1 box Kodiak Blueberry Muffin Mix; To Serve:; Kodiak Mountain Berry Super Fruit Syrup; butter; blueberries; Equipment:; Fire pit
ingredients: Kodiak Mountain Berry Super Fruit Syrup
instructions: Light a fire and let it burn down for 1 hour or until you obtain a medium heat.
Slice the tops off the apples and set aside. Using a corer, core the apples three-quarters of the way through, but keep the bases intact. Scoop out most of the apple flesh and roughly chop.

Add the apple and lemon zest to the muffin mix and make up the batter according to the packet instructions. Spoon the batter into the hollowed-out apples and place the apple lids on top. Wrap the apples in foil.
Use a shovel to make space among the coals away from the center of the fire. Add the apples, shovel some coals on top and cook for 15-20 minutes, until soft.
Unwrap the apples and serve with Kodiak Fruit Syrup, soft butter, and a few blueberries.

name: Asparagus And Goat Cheese Frittata
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1/4 cup olive oil; 1 small red onion, sliced; 12 asparagus stalks, bottoms trimmed; 10 large eggs; 3 tablespoons Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1/2 teaspoon baking powder; 1/4 teaspoon salt; 1/4 teaspoon cracked black pepper; 1 tablespoon fresh chives, chopped; 1/4 cup goat cheese crumbles
ingredients: 3 tablespoons Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350° F and coat a standard pie dish with butter or baking spray.
In a pan over medium heat, sauté the red onion in the olive oil until soft, then remove from heat.
In the same pan, sauté the asparagus over medium heat for about 2 minutes, until bright green, then remove from heat.
Place the sautéed onions and asparagus into the prepared baking dish and spread evenly.
Add the eggs, Kodiak mix, baking powder, salt, pepper, and chives to a blender and blend on low until smooth.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables and sprinkle the goat cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, or until the center is set and cooked through.

Spoon or pipe batter into the greased doughnut pan.

Dip or drizzle over the top of the cooled doughnuts. Top with Halloween sprinkles.

name: Christmas Tree Waffles
description: Need a festive breakfast that will put a smile on your cub's face come Christmas morning – AND tame their wild stomach growls? Look no further, these Christmas Tree Waffles make a fun addition to your holiday menu and require just a few drops of food coloring to create. But why stop there? Let the kids decorate their delicious trees with sprinkles, fresh fruit, syrup, or icing. With help from Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes, not only do these Christmas Tree Waffles taste delicious, but they also pack in wholesome nutrition from whole grains and protein – but we won't tell them that. 😉
product: Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
base: 1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix; 1 cup water; 1 tablespoon oil; 4-5 drops green food coloring; Assorted Christmas sprinkles
ingredients: 1 cup Kodiak Buttermilk Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix
instructions: Stir the Kodiak mix, water, and oil together until combined.
Add food coloring and stir until the batter turns vibrant green.
Pour 1/2 cup of the green batter into a heated and greased waffle round waffle iron. Close the iron and cook according to the waffle iron's instructions.
Remove the waffle and cut it into 4 pieces. Form a tree shape by layering the waffle quarters over one another with the pointed corner toward the top.
Repeat with the remaining batter.
Decorate waffles with holiday sprinkles and serve warm with syrup.
